November 10, 1939. Morning Transl .tion. 


Shun Pao, Sin Wan Fao, Chinese- merican Daily News, Ta Mei Pao: 


FOREIGN BANKS IGNORE BAN OR TRANSPORTATION OF JEGAL TEND_R 


In an attempt to push foiward the circulation 
of Hwa Shing Bank notes, Li Chi-nan (4 x he 
Superintendent of the Shanghai Maritime stoms, recently 
requested the Consuls of warious foreign Powers in Shanghai 
and Mr. Lawford, Commissioner of the Shanghai Maritime 
Customs, to impose a ban on the import of Chinese legal 
tender notes. 

ir. Lawford has not accepted the request 
of the Customs Superintendent for he has not so far issued 
any order banning the import of Chinese legal tender notes. 
However, owing to special circumstances in Shanghai, it 
is feared that the ban may be realized as witness the 
enforcement of the acceptance of Hwa Shing Bank notes by 
the Shanghai Customs on September 1 despite the fact that 
the Customs Commissioner had not issued any order in this 
connection. For this reason, transportation of Chinese 
legal tender notes by the Central Bank of China, the Bank 
of China, the Bank of Communications and the Fo-mers Bank 
of China in future may experience some troubles 

Following the withdrawal of Chinese troops 
from Shanghai, the Central Bank of China and three others 
immediately ceased transportation of Chinese legal tender 
notes to Shanghai. With a view to meeting the demand 
of the Shanghai market, various foreign banks in Shanghai 
made arrangements with the head offices of the abovementioned 
four banks to undertake the transportation to Shanghai of 
Chinese legal tender noteSe For instance, the 8.8. 
President Pierce of the American President Line has 
arrived in Shanghai with $10,000,000 in Chinese legal tender 
owned by the Chase Bank, an American-owned concern. The 
Customs Superintendent attempted to hinder this transportation 
but owing to foreign ownership, the consignment was safely 
discharged. The various foreign banks have decided to 
ignore the demand of the Customs Superintendent. 

According to information obtained by a 
reporter of the Sing Sung News Agency (tr syiimtt) from local 
banking circles, the amount of Ghinese legal tender notes 
now circulating in the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai is 
very large and is sufficient to meet requirements. Should 
a check be forcibly placed upon the transportation of 
Chinese legal tender to Shanghai, local residents would be 
in no way affected. The Chinese legal tender transported 
to Shanghai by foreign banks was intended absolutely for 
international trading purposes, and in case the Customs 
Superintendent put a stop to such transportation, various 
foreign Powers would sustain heavy losses in their tradings 
and would undoubtedly lodge strong protests. 

Information from foreign banking circles 
reveals that the legal tender transported to Shanghai is 
owned by them and the Customs @uperintendent has absolutely 
no right to interfere with it. 

With the drop in the fcreign exchange and 
the depreciation in the value of gold as a result of the 
turn for the better in China's tradings with foreign Powers, 
SBpeculators dare not further manipulate the market and 
the latter has been restored to normal. Following an 


attempt of the Customs Superintendent to put a stop to 


the transportation of Chinese legal tender to Shanghat, 
certain speculators thought to resume their activities; 
they spread certain rumours put it is believed that they 


will meet with failure.

CUSTOMS INTEND TO STOP IMPORT AND ORT OF LEGAL TENDE 


pS 


The Customs is now contemplating taking a 
further step towards the control of commerce. 

Acoording to information secured yesterday 
by a reporter of this paper from diplomatic circles, Li 
Elieerionan ( 9 ), Superintendent of Customs appointed 
by the Reformed overnment," has sent out copies of an 
official notification to the local foreign Consulates to 
the effect that hereafter import and export of legal tender 
notes will be prohibited. The notification, however, was 
ignored by the local Consular authorities as it came from 
an organ that has so far been given no official recognition. 

according to a certain local business magnate, 
this attempt is being made by the puppet authorities in the 
hope of bringing about a decrease in the number of legal 
tender notes in circulation in Shanghai, so that the Hwa 
Shing notes can be circulated in their stead. This is 
apparently another example of the poisonous policy of 
economic aggression aimed at tlhe destruction of comme ce 
in Shanghai, especially the inteacsts of third party nations. 

No information is availac’e as to the contents 
of the notification as the officials of the Customs refused 
to made any statement. However, they have intimated that 
any breach of this order will result in the confiscation 
of the legal tender notes being transported.

November 10, 1939. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao:

FOREIGN BANKS IGNORE BAN ON TRANSPORTATION OF LEGAL TENDER

In an attempt to push forward the circulation of Hwa Shing Bank notes, Li Chi-nan (李遲南), Superintendent of the Shanghai Maritime Customs, recently requested the Consuls of various foreign Powers in Shanghai and Mr. Lawford, Commissioner of the Shanghai Maritime Customs, to impose a ban on the import of Chinese legal tender notes.

Mr. Lawford has not accepted the request of the Customs Superintendent for he has not so far issued any order banning the import of Chinese legal tender notes. However, owing to special circumstances in Shanghai, it is feared that the ban may be realized as witness the enforcement of the acceptance of Hwa Shing Bank notes by the Shanghai Customs on September 1 despite the fact that the Customs Commissioner had not issued any order in this connection. For this reason, transportation of Chinese legal tender notes by the Central Bank of China, the Bank of China, the Bank of Communications and the Farmers Bank of China in future may experience some trouble.

Following the withdrawal of Chinese troops from Shanghai, the Central Bank of China and three others immediately ceased transportation of Chinese legal tender notes to Shanghai. With a view to meeting the demand of the Shanghai market, various foreign banks in Shanghai made arrangements with the head offices of the abovementioned four banks to undertake the transportation to Shanghai of Chinese legal tender notes. For instance, the s.s. President Pierce of the American President Line has arrived in Shanghai with $10,000,000 in Chinese legal tender owned by the Chase Bank, an American-owned concern. The Customs Superintendent attempted to hinder this transportation but owing to foreign ownership, the consignment was safely discharged. The various foreign banks have decided to ignore the demand of the Customs Superintendent.

According to information obtained by a reporter of the Sing Sung News Agency (新聲社) from local banking circles, the amount of Chinese legal tender notes now circulating in the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai is very large and is sufficient to meet requirements. Should a check be forcibly placed upon the transportation of Chinese legal tender to Shanghai, local residents would be in no way affected. The Chinese legal tender transported to Shanghai by foreign banks was intended absolutely for international trading purposes, and in case the Customs Superintendent put a stop to such transportation, various Foreign Powers would sustain heavy losses in their tradings and would undoubtedly lodge strong protests.

Information from foreign banking circles reveals that the legal tender transported to Shanghai is owned by them and the Customs Superintendent has absolutely no right to interfere with it.

With the drop in the foreign exchange and the depreciation in the value of gold as a result of the turn for the better in China's tradings with foreign Powers, speculators dare not further manipulate the market and the latter has been restored to normal. Following an

1939年11月10日。晨间译稿。

《申报》、《新闻报》、《中美日报》、《大美晚报》：

外商银行无视法币运输禁令

为推进华兴银行钞票的流通，上海海关监督李迟南 (Li Chi-nan) 近日请求驻沪各国领事及上海海关税务司劳福德先生 (Mr. Lawford) 禁止进口中国法币钞票。

劳福德先生未接受海关监督的请求，因此迄今未发布任何禁止进口中国法币钞票的命令。然而，鉴于上海的特殊情况，恐怕禁令终将实施，正如尽管海关税务司未就此发布任何命令，上海海关仍于9月1日强制执行接受华兴银行钞票一样。因此，中央银行、中国银行、交通银行和中国农民银行今后运输中国法币钞票可能会遇到一些麻烦。

随着中国军队撤出上海，中央银行及其他三家银行立即停止向上海运输中国法币钞票。为满足上海市场的需求，在沪各外商银行与上述四家银行的总行达成协议，承担向上海运输中国法币钞票的任务。例如，美商美华轮船公司 (American President Line) 的“皮尔斯总统”号轮船 (s.s. President Pierce) 已抵达上海，载有美资大通银行 (Chase Bank) 所有的价值1000万美元的中国法币。海关监督试图阻碍此次运输，但由于货物属外资所有，该批货物得以安全卸货。各外商银行已决定无视海关监督的要求。

据新声社 (Sing Sung News Agency) 记者从本地银行界获得的消息，目前在上海公共租界流通的中国法币钞票数量巨大，足以满足需求。如果强行检查运往上海的法币，当地居民不会受到任何影响。外商银行运往上海的法币完全用于国际贸易目的，如果海关监督阻止此类运输，各国列强在贸易中将遭受重大损失，并无疑会提出强烈抗议。

来自外商银行界的消息显示，运往上海的法币归他们所有，海关监督绝对无权干涉。

随着中外贸易好转导致外汇下跌和金价贬值，投机者不敢再操纵市场，市场已恢复正常。继

November 8, 1939. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao and Chinese-American Daily
News :-

CUSTOMS INTEND TO STOP IMPORT AND EXPORT OF LEGAL TENDER
NOTES

The Customs is now contemplating taking a
further step towards the control of commerce.
According to information secured yesterday
by a reporter of this paper from diplomatic circles, Li
Chien-nan (李建南 ), Superintendent of Customs appointed
by the Reformed Government," has sent out copies of an
official notification to the local foreign Consulates to
the effect that hereafter import and export of legal tender
notes will be prohibited. The notification, however, was
ignored by the local Consular authorities as it came from
an organ that has so far been given no official recognition.
According to a certain local business magnate,
this attempt is being made by the puppet authorities in the
hope of bringing about a decrease in the number of legal
tender notes in circulation in Shanghai, so that the Hwa
Shing notes can be circulated in their stead. This is
apparently another example of the poisonous policy of
economic aggression aimed at the destruction of commerce
in Shanghai, especially the interests of third party nations.
No information is available as to the contents
of the notification as the officials of the Customs refused
to made any statement. However, they have intimated that
any breach of this order will result in the confiscation
of the legal tender notes being transported.

No Confirmation
obtainable
I - - -
HYR

1939年11月8日。晨间译稿。

《大美晚报》、《新闻报》、《申报》和《中美日报》：

海关拟禁止法币进出口

海关正考虑采取进一步措施控制商业。
据本报记者昨日从外交界获得的消息，维新政府任命的海关监督李建南 (Li Chien-nan) 已向当地外国领事馆发出官方通知副本，称此后将禁止法币钞票的进出口。然而，当地领事当局忽视了该通知，因为它来自一个迄今未获正式承认的机构。据当地一位商界巨头称，傀儡当局此举是希望减少上海流通的法币数量，以便用华兴钞票取而代之。这显然是旨在破坏上海商业，特别是第三方国家利益的经济侵略毒政策的又一例证。
由于海关官员拒绝发表任何声明，无法得知通知的内容。然而，他们暗示，任何违反此命令的行为将导致被运输的法币钞票被没收。

无法获得
确认
I - - -

NOV 8 1939

Big Banknote
Consignment
Is Detained

Released By Customs
After Negotiations
By Chase Bank

BAN PLACED ON FAPI
IMPORTS, EXPORTS

As the first official step in
carrying out the new Customs
Notification, issued under the
signature of Mr. Li Chien-nan,
Superintendent of the Shang-
hai Customs appointed by the
Reformed Government of Nan-
king, Customs authorities yes-
terday seized a consignment of
several million Chinese bank-
notes, "fapi," brought from
Hongkong aboard the s.s. Pres-
ident Pierce for the Chase
Bank.

After protests from the bank
officials and other authorities and
lengthy negotiations, the banknotes
were passed through and turned
over to the Chase Bank. However,
the Customs authorities are report-
ed to have stated that strict ad-
herence would henceforth be made
to the order forbidding the export or
import of Chinese banknotes.

The seizure came as a surprise, as
since the Reformed Government
have had a Commissioner in the
local Customs no ban had been
exercised on the import or export
of notes. Yesterday morning, how-
ever, Mr. Li Chien-nan forwarded
to all local consuls a notification
stating that the Reformed Govern-
ment had issued an order forbidding
the importing or exporting of
Chinese banknotes without a special
licence.

Although only forwarded to mem-
bers of the Consular Body yester-
day morning, the notification was
dated November 4, and it was
probably on this authority that the
Customs officers had acted in seizing
the notes destined for the Chase
Bank.

Licence Required

Although the full text of the
Customs Notification has not been
made public, it is understood that
it provides that currency secretly
transported is to be detained. In
special cases permits will be grant-
ed through the proper channels, the
notification states.

Li

1939年11月8日

大批钞票
货物
被扣留

经大通银行
交涉后
由海关放行

禁止
法币
进出口

作为执行南京维新政府任命的上海海关监督李建南先生签署的新海关通告的第一项官方步骤，海关当局昨日扣押了一批由“皮尔斯总统”号轮船从香港运抵、 destined for 大通银行的数百万中国钞票（“法币”）。

经过银行官员和其他当局的抗议以及长时间的谈判，这批钞票获准通过并移交给大通银行。然而，据报道，海关当局表示，今后将严格执行禁止中国钞票出口或进口的命令。

此次扣押令人意外，因为自维新政府在当地海关派驻税务司以来，一直未对钞票的进出口实施禁令。然而，昨天上午，李建南先生向所有当地领事发送了一份通知，称维新政府已发布命令，禁止在没有特别许可证的情况下进口或出口中国钞票。

虽然该通知直到昨天上午才发送给领事团成员，但其日期为11月4日，海关官员很可能是依据此授权扣押了 destined for 大通银行的钞票。

需许可证

虽然海关通告的全文尚未公布，但据悉其中规定，秘密运输的货币将被扣留。通知称，在特殊情况下，将通过适当渠道发放许可证。

李

News Digest and other local newspapers :-
Morning Translation
November 9, 1938.

THE AFFAIR OF THE LOCAL CUSTOMS
Mr. Lawford, Commissioner of the Shanghai
Maritime Customs, has denied that the Customs has changed
its flag. Yesterday Mr. Lawford issued an order declaring
a holiday in accordance with the orders of the National
Government. All internal and external affairs of the
Customs will continue to be conducted according to the
orders and wishes of the National Government.
Watch duties in the Customs House have been
taken over by foreign officers who will do their best to
prevent a recurrence of the recent flag incident.

News Digest publishes the following two letters :-

Two Open Letters To Customs Officers

(1) Officers of the Shanghai Maritime Customs:
The incident on November 4 is intolerable.
We are indignant at the shameful act of the Japanese and
their running dogs; at the same time, we respect your
loyalty to the country and your spirit of struggle.
The humiliation is not only intolerable to
the Customs officers who have to pass under the bogus
flag daily, but also to the 4,000,000 residents of
Shanghai.
The vicious Japanese are unsatiable. They
will want to seize other rights once they have seized the
Customs. Therefore by protecting the Customs rights, we
are protecting other rights also and every Chinese should
oppose the changing of the flag by the Customs.
As a result of her policy of compromise,
Great Britain is now being challenged by Japan. We hope
Britain will reconsider her policy.
Customs officers! It is glorious to fight
for the country. Let us die rather than submit to insult.
We are a group of primary school teachers in
Shanghai. We will unite all primary school teachers and
children in Shanghai to support you!
Wishing you victory.
Tai Kwei (戴桂), Wu Wan-tseng (吴万增),
Tseng Sung (曾松), Li Ying (李英),
Tseng Ching (曾静), Kun Loh-sih (昆洛士),
Chui Zung-zai (崔宗载), Hwa Ching (华清),
Chow Yung (周永) and Li Ming (黎明).
November 6.

(2) The Brave Chinese Officers of the Customs:
Mr. --- has told us that the shameful five-
barred flag has been hoisted over the Customs House. How
distressing is this! We are waiting to see you take
revenge. We hope you will unite and deal a blow to the
shameless traitors and the Japanese Imperialists.
Brethren, you are our vanguards and we are
your support. We want to see our national flag again.
We went to save China.
From a little friend, Liang Yuan-tao (梁元道).

《新闻摘要》及其他本地报纸：-
晨间译稿
1938年11月9日。

本地海关事件

上海海关税务司劳福德（Lawford）先生否认海关已更换旗帜。昨日，劳福德先生根据国民政府的命令发布通告，宣布放假。海关的一切内外事务将继续按照国民政府的命令和意愿进行。
海关大楼的守卫职责已由外籍职员接管，他们将尽力防止近期换旗事件再次发生。

《新闻摘要》刊登以下两封信：-

致海关职员的两封公开信

(1) 上海海关职员们：
11月4日的事件令人无法容忍。我们对日本人及其走狗的无耻行径感到愤慨；同时，我们尊重你们对国家的忠诚和斗争精神。
这种耻辱不仅让每日不得不从伪旗下走过的海关职员难以忍受，也让上海四百万居民难以忍受。
邪恶的日本人贪得无厌。他们在夺取海关之后，还会想要夺取其他权利。因此，保护海关权利，也就是保护其他权利，每个中国人都应反对海关换旗。
由于实行妥协政策，英国正受到日本的挑战。我们希望英国重新考虑其政策。
海关职员们！为国争光。宁死不受辱。
我们是上海的一群小学教师。我们将团结上海所有小学教师和儿童支持你们！
祝胜利。
戴桂、吴万增、曾松、李英、
曾静、昆洛士（音译）、
崔宗载、华清、
周永和黎明。
11月6日。

(2) 勇敢的海关中国职员们：
--- 先生告诉我们，耻辱的五色旗已悬挂在海关大楼上。这是多么令人痛心！我们等待着看你们复仇。希望你们团结起来，打击无耻的汉奸和日本帝国主义者。
兄弟们，你们是先锋，我们是你们的后盾。我们要再次看到我们的国旗。
我们去拯救中国。
来自一位小朋友，梁元道。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

AUG 31 1939

Important Customs
Ruling

Dues Must Be Paid in Hwa
Hsing or Standard Dollars
From Tomorrow

Payment of Customs duties in
Hwa Hsing bank notes is now a fact.
It is officially announced that from
tomorrow "payments of Customs
duties in Customs Gold Unit notes
or in Customs Gold unit cheques
will not be accepted, and all Customs
duties, dues and fees will either be
paid in Hwa Hsing Dollars and in
Standard Dollars." The "Standard
Dollars" here mean legal tender
notes issued by Chungking and as
they are quoted at about two pence
below Hwa Hsing notes issued by
the Hongkew institution traders are
therefore required to pay more than
before.

Interviewed, Mr Li Chien-nan,
Superintendent of Customs (Re-
formed Government appointee) who
issued the order, stated that he did
not make any distinction between
Hwa Hsing notes and Standard
Dollars asserting that he merely
wanted to collect Customs duties
on a dollar-for-6-pence basis so as
to cover the losses sustained by his
administration as a result of the
drop of the value of the legal tender
notes.

And so it is mentioned in his
order that the duty collecting
rate will remain unaffected until the
value of local currency depreciated
to below 6d. and then the duty
collecting rate will be adjusted to
meet the difference between 6d. and
the market rate for local currency.
In other words, it was explained,
even should the Hwa Hsing note
drop to below 6 pence (which is
its value at present) Customs duties
will be collected on the fixed 6-pence-
for-a-dollar basis. One Customs Gold
Unit is worth $2.396 (officially
equivalent to 40 cents in American
currency) but if the Hwa Hsing
note drops to below 6 pence its
holder will pay "$3 something",
Mr. Li explained.

Text of Order

The exchange rate of the Customs
Gold Unit with the Hwa Hsing
Dollar and the Standard Dollar
together with the exchange rate
between the latter two currencies
will be notified at the Customs.
The full text of the order is as
follows:

The public is hereby notified that in
accordance with Government instruc-
tions effective from September 1, 1939
payments of Customs duties in Customs
Gold Unit notes or in Customs Gold
Unit cheques will not be accepted, and
all Customs duties, dues and fees will
either be paid in Hwa Hsing Dollars or
in Standard Dollars.

The Customs Gold Unit will remain
unchanged but no account will be taken
of the depreciation of local currency
down to a minimum of 6d. That is to
say, the duty collecting rate will remain
unaffected until the value of local cur-
rency depreciated to below 6d and then
the duty collecting rate will be adjusted
to meet the difference between 6d. and
the market rate for local currency. The
exchange rate of the Customs Gold Unit
with the Hwa Hsing Dollar and the
Standard Dollar together with the ex-
change rate between the latter two cur-
rencies will be notified daily at the
Customs.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年8月31日

重要海关
裁决

明日起关税须以
华兴银行券或法币支付

以华兴银行券缴纳关税现已成为事实。
官方宣布，从明天起，“不再接受以海关金单位钞票或海关金单位支票缴纳关税，所有关税、捐税和费用必须以华兴银行券或‘标准元’支付。”这里的“标准元”是指重庆发行的法定货币纸币，由于其报价比虹口机构发行的华兴银行券低约两便士，因此商人需支付的金额比以往更多。

在接受采访时，发布该命令的海关监督（维新政府任命）李建南（Li Chien-nan）先生表示，他并不区分华兴银行券和标准元，声称他只是希望按每美元兑6便士的基础征收关税，以弥补其管理部门因法定货币纸币贬值而遭受的损失。

因此，他的命令中提到，在当地货币价值贬值至低于6便士之前，征税税率将保持不变；此后，征税税率将进行调整，以弥补6便士与当地货币市场汇率之间的差额。换句话说，据解释，即使华兴银行券跌至低于6便士（即其当前价值），关税仍将按固定的每美元兑6便士的基础征收。一个海关金单位值2.396美元（官方等值于40美分），但如果华兴银行券跌至低于6便士，持有者将支付“3点几美元”，李先生解释道。

命令全文

海关金单位与华兴银行券及标准元的汇率，以及后两种货币之间的汇率，将在海关公布。
命令全文如下：

特此公告，根据政府指令，自1939年9月1日起生效，不再接受以海关金单位钞票或海关金单位支票缴纳关税，所有关税、捐税和费用必须以华兴银行券或标准元支付。

海关金单位将保持不变，但在当地货币贬值至最低6便士之前，不予考虑其贬值因素。也就是说，在当地货币价值贬值至低于6便士之前，征税税率将保持不变；此后，征税税率将进行调整，以弥补6便士与当地货币市场汇率之间的差额。海关金单位与华兴银行券及标准元的汇率，以及后两种货币之间的汇率，将每日在海关公布。

Decision

fapi, the Shanghai correspondent of
the commercial daily "Chugai
Shogyo" said.

Since the administration of the
Maritime Customs in Central China,
including Shanghai, had been taken
over by the Reformed Government
it was but natural that all Customs
dues should be paid in notes of the
Hua Hsing Commercial Bank, legal
tender of the new Nanking Govern-
ment, the correspondent said.

He pointed out that heretofore the
Nanking Government had taken no
action regarding the payments be-
cause Hua Hsing notes and fapi were
exchanged at par while the circula-
tion of Hua Hsing notes was limited.

Since June, however, the exchange
rate of the Chungking dollar had
slumped severely, which resulted in
a marked decline in Customs re-
venue, the correspondent recalled.
He pointed out that the new regula-
tions would result in a 50 per cent
increase in Customs dues to those
who paid in fapi, while they would
mean a 50 per cent. reduction to
those who paid in Japanese yen. He
said the regulations would rectify
an unfair situation arising from de-
valuation of fapi and pegging of it
at one shilling and twopence, which
heretofore subjected Japanese mer-
chandise to an unfairly high Cus-
toms tariff.—Domei.

《上海泰晤士报》，

1939年9月12日

海关
付款
决定

因收入下降
改用华兴银行券支付

东京，9月11日电。——商业日报《中外商业》驻上海记者称，强制要求华中港口以华兴银行券缴纳海关捐税，主要是为了防止因法币贬值导致海关收入减少。

该记者称，自从包括上海在内的华中地区海关行政权被维新政府接管后，所有海关捐税自然应以新南京政府的法定货币——华兴商业银行的纸币支付。

他指出，此前南京政府未对此类付款采取行动，是因为华兴银行券与法币平价兑换，且华兴银行券的流通量有限。

然而，该记者回顾说，自6月以来，重庆元汇率严重暴跌，导致海关收入显著下降。他指出，新规定将使以法币支付者的海关捐税增加50%，而以日元支付者的捐税则减少50%。他说，这些规定将纠正因法币贬值并将其固定在1先令2便士而产生的不公平状况，此前这使得日本商品承受了不公平的高额海关关税。——同盟社。

Reported taking over of the Bank of China Customs Collection Office by the Japanese Authorities.

Sir,

Information that the Bank of China Customs Collection Office was about to be taken over by the Japanese Authorities and that trouble was anticipated was passed to the officer in charge of Central District by the A.C. (Divisional) through the Divisional Officer at 10.30 a.m. August 31.

The Chief of the River Police was subsequently interviewed and requested to disclose any information he or members of his staff possessed regarding the rumoured impending coup. A.C. (Divisional) was informed and instructed that precautionary measures be taken immediately in the vicinity of the Customs House.

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
SEP 5 1939
24554
82/5

Another Customs
Difficulty

Chungking's Reduction in
Duty Cannot Be Carried Out
Here, Press Believes

Although the Chinese people as a
whole and foreign traders should feel
relieved to learn that the Chinese
Government at Chungking has now
announced a reduction of Customs
duties levied on "non-banned" foreign
goods, meaning goods which are not
luxuries, Chinese press circles saw
yesterday that it would be difficult to
carry out the new order in Shanghai
as the Customs office here is not
within Chungking's influence.

Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance,
has, it is reported, instructed Customs
commissioners to carry out the order
and also notified all provincial and
district Chambers of Commerce. The
purpose of Dr Kung's new order, it
is explained, is to enable the people
to obtain foreign goods which China
can not produce at cheaper prices as
a reward for the people's support
during the hostilities.

Dr. Kung's order has reduced the
present Customs duties imposed on
these goods by one-third and the
order will hold good until the end
of the hostilities. The order, how-
ever, will not be applied to those
goods the importation of which were
banned in another order which be-
came effective on July 1 of this year.
It will be recalled that in the previous
order more than 200 kinds of foreign
goods (luxuries) were prohibited from
being imported into this country.

The Customs duty collecting office
in the Shanghai Customs office has
just been taken over by the Japanese
at the request of Mr. Li Chien-nan,
Superintendent of the Customs ap-
pointed by the new Nanking regime.
Doubt has therefore been expressed
by the Chinese press that they will
be able to carry out Dr. Kung's new
order. People who live in the in-
terior under Chungking's control,
however, are favoured by the order
and it is learned that they should feel
much relieved because prices of for-
eign goods in the interior are much
higher than those quoted in Shanghai.

《字林西报》
1939年9月5日
24554
82/5

另一海关难题

报界认为重庆减免关税令无法在此执行

尽管全体中国人民和外国商人在得知重庆中国政府现已宣布降低对“非禁止”外国货物（即非奢侈品）征收的关税后应感到宽慰，但中国新闻界昨日认为，由于上海的海关办事处不在重庆的影响范围内，新命令在上海难以执行。

据报道，财政部长孔祥熙博士已指示海关税务司执行该命令，并通知了各省及各地区商会。据解释，孔博士新命令的目的是使人民能够以更低的价格获得中国无法生产的外国货物，以此作为对人民在敌对期间支持的回报。

孔博士的命令将这些货物现行的关税降低了三分之一，该命令有效期至敌对行动结束。然而，该命令不适用于根据今年7月1日生效的另一项命令禁止进口的货物。回想起来，在前一项命令中，有200多种外国货物（奢侈品）被禁止进口到本国。

上海海关内的关税征收处刚刚应新任南京政权委任的海关税务司李健南先生的要求被日本人接管。因此，中国报界对能否执行孔博士的新命令表示怀疑。然而，生活在重庆控制下的内地民众受惠于该命令，据悉他们应感到大大宽慰，因为内地的外国货物价格远高于上海的报价。

CHINA PRESS.

SEP 5 1939

Customs Revenue Of
£2,500,000 Deposited
With Yokohama Bank

During the first half year of the
current year, the Shanghai Cus-
toms collected $72,000,000 as Cus-
toms revenues. All this money was
deposited with the Yokohama
Specie Bank. At the average rate
of 6d., it was estimated that the
Japanese bank obtained during the
first six months of the year no less
than £2,500,000 according to the
Sin Wan Pao, released by China
News and Views Digest.
Customs revenue for the second
half year is estimated to be $48,-
000,000 because of the general de-
crease of foreign trade. According
to the present rate of exchange,
the Japanese bank may obtain
£750,000. With the introduction of
the "Hwa Hsing" notes as the me-
dium for the payment of Customs
duties, it is expected that the
Customs duty will be increased by
55 per cent and that the revenue
will also be increased by 55 per
cent.
With the outbreak of hostilities
in Europe, it is believed that the
volume of trade will be further re-
duced and much less revenue can
be collected by the Japanese bank.
It may be noted that on August
31, the local Customs collected as
much as $2,000,000 as import and
export duties But on September 1,
the total revenue was only $30,000.

《大美晚报》。

1939年9月5日

250万英镑关税收入存入横滨银行

在今年上半年，上海海关征收了7,200万美元的关税收入。所有这些钱都存入了横滨正金银行。据《新闻报》发布、由《中外日报文摘》转载的消息，按平均汇率6便士计算，估计这家日本银行在今年前六个月获得了不少于250万英镑的收入。
由于对外贸易普遍减少，预计下半年的关税收入为4,800万美元。按当前汇率计算，这家日本银行可能获得75万英镑。随着“华兴”银行券作为缴纳关税的媒介引入，预计关税额将增加55%，收入也将增加55%。
随着欧洲敌对行动的爆发，人们相信贸易量将进一步减少，这家日本银行能征收的收入也会少得多。值得注意的是，8月31日，当地海关征收的进出口关税高达200万美元，但9月1日，总收入仅为3万美元。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

SEP 5 1939

REDUCED RATES ON
LOCAL IMPORTS

Chungking Instruction
Not Expected To Be
Enforced Here

In connection with the recent
order issued by the Ministry of
Finance of the Chinese National
Government, requesting all the
Chinese Maritime Customs Ad-
ministrations to reduce the present
import duties by one-third, it was
reported yesterday that there was
no likelihood of the order being
enforced in the occupied areas.

An identical order was reported
to have been received from the
Ministry of Finance by Mr H. L.
Lawford, Commissioner of Customs
in Shanghai, but there appears to
be difficulties in enforcing the order
to the Shanghai Chinese Maritime
Customs owing to "abnormal con-
ditions" prevailing in these parts,
as the Japanese military authori-
ties are inclined to the view that
the Shanghai area is under mili-
tary occupation.

The order of the Ministry stated
that imports which are not under
bar may be permitted to enter the
country at reduced duties by one-
third of its existing rates.

《上海泰晤士报》。

1939年9月5日

本地进口税率降低

预计重庆指令不会在此执行

关于中国国民政府财政部最近发布的命令，要求所有中国海关管理局将现行进口关税降低三分之一，昨日据报道，该命令在被占领地区执行的可能性不大。

据报道，上海海关税务司劳福德（H. L. Lawford）先生也收到了财政部发出的相同命令，但由于这些地区 prevailing 的“异常情况”，在上海中国海关执行该命令似乎存在困难，因为日本军事当局倾向于认为上海地区处于军事占领之下。

财政部的命令指出，未受禁令限制的进口货物可以按现有税率降低三分之一的优惠关税进入本国。

September 4, 1939. Afternoon Translation.
Chinese American Daily News (3/9/39):-

HWA SHING BANK NOTES AND THE CUSTOMS

The Revenue Department of the Central Bank of China the day before yesterday was forcibly occupied by Japanese who compelled the Customs Authorities to collect Hwa Shing Bank Notes in payment of its duties, despite the fact that the Commissioner has been negotiating with the Japanese authorities concerned and has suggested to them a reasonable method in dealing with the matter. These negotiations failed as support was not received from various nations, especially the British who have adopted a pacific attitude. At present the Customs are being forced to accept Hwa Shing Bank notes in payment of duties, the Customs authorities however have not actually agreed to this matter.

The Japanese wished the Customs authorities to issue a notification to the effect that Hwa Shing Bank notes only would be accepted but this has been refused, apparently as a protest against the Japanese.

The Customs continued to collect duties in Legal Tender. When Customs duties amount to more than $100, only the cheques of foreign banks and Yokohama Specie Bank are accepted by Customs.

Increased burden of Chinese and foreign merchants.

Yesterday the Customs authorities ordered that duties on all export goods be collected in Legal Tender, the amount due being first reckoned in Hwa Shing money, and the import goods in Hwa Shing notes only.

It is learned that on 31/8/39 the Revenue Department of the Central Bank of China collected altogether 2 million dollars in payment of import and export duties, but after the Department being occupied by the Japanese the amount of import duties collected in one day dropped to $30,000.

Since the staff employees of the Revenue Department of the Central Bank of China had been expelled by the Japanese, the official in charge of this Department, Mr. Shen, has asked for instructions from the Shanghai Branch of the Central Bank of China as to their future and in the meantime has temporarily transferred the staff in question to the Shanghai Branch Office until instructions are received from the Head Office, Chungking.

Today the Customs House is still strictly guarded by Chinese and Indian police and detectives. At the entrance of the Revenue Office there is a number of British and Japanese detectives, it appears that the situation is rather tense.

Central China Daily News:

The Central Bank of China and other banks in this locality have all expressed the impossibility of accepting Hwa Shing Bank notes.

In an interview with our reporter yesterday, a certain banker made the following statement:- "Concerning the acceptance of Hwa Shing bank notes by the local Customs, the local Bankers' Association will discuss the matter today and see reports received from various banks. We may tell you frankly that all banks in this locality have determined not to accept Hwa Shing bank notes. A number of native banks are accepting Hwa Shing notes for transactions only but they do not use them in the market.

1939年9月4日。下午译文。
《中美日报》（1939年9月3日）：-

华兴银行券与海关

中国银行收入处前天被日本人强行占领，迫使海关当局收取华兴银行券作为关税支付，尽管税务司一直在与相关日本当局谈判，并向他们提出了处理此事的合理方法。由于未得到各国支持，特别是采取了绥靖态度的英国，这些谈判失败了。目前，海关被迫接受华兴银行券支付关税，但海关当局实际上并未同意此事。

日本人希望海关当局发布通知，声明仅接受华兴银行券，但这已被拒绝，显然是为了抗议日本人。

海关继续以法币收取关税。当关税金额超过100美元时，海关只接受外国银行和横滨正金银行的支票。

中外商人负担加重。

昨日，海关当局命令所有出口货物的关税以法币收取，金额先按华兴货币计算，而进口货物仅收华兴银行券。

据悉，1939年8月31日，中国银行收入处共收取200万美元的进出口关税，但在该部门被日本人占领后，一日之内收取的进口关税金额降至3万美元。

由于中国银行收入处的职员被日本人驱逐，该部门负责人沈先生已向中国银行上海分行请示后续安排，同时暂时将有关职员调至上海分行办公，直至收到重庆总行的指示。

今天，海关大楼仍由中国和印度警察及侦探严密守卫。在收入处入口处有多名英国和日本侦探，局势似乎相当紧张。

《华中日报》：

中国银行及本地其他银行均表示不可能接受华兴银行券。

一位银行家在昨日接受本报记者采访时发表如下声明：“关于本地海关接受华兴银行券一事，本地银行公会今日将讨论此事并查看各家银行收到的报告。我们可以坦率地告诉您，本地所有银行已决定不接受华兴银行券。一些钱庄仅在交易中使用华兴银行券，但不将其用于市场流通。”

September 1, 1939.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

REVENUE OFFICE OF CENTRAL BANK MAY BE TAKEN OVER
BY "REFORMED GOVERNMENT"

As previously reported the "Reformed
Government" has decided that Hwa Shing Bank notes are to be
used when paying Customs duties and other fees. The Central
Bank of China, however, is unwilling to observe the new
order issued by Mr. Li Chien-nan, Superintendent of Customs.
The "Reformed Government", the
Hwa Shing Commercial Bank and the Yokohama Specie Bank,
which are jointly controlling the revenue of the Customs,
have decided to take over the Revenue Office of the Central
Bank of China, which is located at the corner of Szechuen
and Hankow Roads, at 7 a.m. to-day, with an intimation that
the various organs controlled by the Chungking Government
will be deprived of connection with Customs affairs.
The Central Bank of China was
greatly surprised upon learning of the intention of the
"Reformed Government".
The main gate of the Central Bank
of China is being guarded by some ten policemen from the
S.M.P. and the Water Police. The Revenue Office of the
Central Bank will probably be taken over by the "Reformed
Government".

1939年9月1日。

《大陆新报》

中国银行收入处可能被“维新政府”接管

如前所述，“维新政府”已决定在缴纳关税和其他费用时使用华兴银行券。然而，中国银行不愿遵守新任海关税务司李健南先生发布的新命令。“维新政府”、华兴商业银行和横滨正金银行共同控制海关收入，已决定于今日上午7时接管位于四川路与汉口路转角的中国银行收入处，并暗示重庆政府控制的各个机构将被剥夺与海关事务的联系。
中国银行得知“维新政府”的意图后大为震惊。
中国银行正门由约十名工部局警务处和水警警察守卫。中国银行收入处可能会被“维新政府”接管。

Subject Chinese Maritime Customs - Hwa Shing bank notes accepted

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. [Signature]

The Chinese Maritime Customs, 13 The Bund,
commenced on September 1 to accept Hwa Shing bank
notes. The exchange rate on September 1 was as
follows: one Customs Gold unit was equivalent to
$2.50 in Hwa Shing notes or $3.90 in legal tender and
$1 in Hwa Shing note equals to $1.55 in legal tender.
Legal tender is also accepted in payment of Customs
dues, but at the above discount.

The Customs Dues Collection Office hitherto
operated by the Central bank of China was taken over
by some 40 Japanese of the Yokohama Specie bank at
9 a.m. September 1. The former staff of the Central
bank obtained the information of the taking over in
advance and did not appear at their office on the
morning of September 1. No untoward incident
occurred during the taking over.

The Yokohama Specie bank posted a notification
at the Customs Dues Collection Office on September 1.
It reads as follows :-

"It is hereby notified that from date, only the
drafts and cheques guaranteed by Japanese banks,
the Hwa Shing bank and foreign banks will be
accepted. Any person paying Customs dues over
the amount of $100 in legal tender is required
to pay them with the above-mentioned drafts and
cheques. It is hoped that all merchants will
act accordingly.
Yokohama Specie bank.
September 1, 1939."

位于外滩13号的中国海关，自9月1日开始接受华兴银行钞票。9月1日的汇率如下：1海关金单位相当于华兴钞票2.50元，或法币3.90元；1元华兴钞票等于1.55元法币。海关税费亦接受法币支付，但须按上述折扣计算。

此前由中国银行运营的关税征收处，于9月1日上午9时由约40名横滨正金银行的日本职员接管。原中国银行职员提前获知接管消息，故9月1日上午未出现在办公室。接管过程中未发生任何意外事件。

横滨正金银行于9月1日在关税征收处张贴通告。内容如下：

“特此通知，即日起，仅接受由日本银行、华兴银行及外国银行担保的汇票和支票。凡以法币支付超过100元海关税费者，须以上述汇票和支票支付。望各商号遵照执行。
横滨正金银行。

CHINA PRESS
SEP 2 1939
24458
New Customs
Ruling Causes
Uncertainties

Complete Expulsion Of
Foreign Trade Said
Ultimate Result

HUA HSING NOTES
PUT INTO USE

Difficulty Of Getting
Foreign Exchange
Foreseen

Foreign business in Shanghai is
doomed.
This prediction was made by a
prominent businessman in an
interviewed with THE CHINA PRESS
when he was asked to comment on
the new Shanghai Maritime Cus-
toms ruling requiring the payment
of Customs duties, dues and fees
in Hua Hsing banknotes.
The ruling was put into effect
by the Japanese yesterday when
they replaced the staff of the
Customs Collection Office, employees
of the Central Bank, with 33 clerks
from the Yokohama Specie Bank.
When the Collection Office, amid
great confusion, opened yesterday
morning, posters were put up
around the building that payments
of $100 or more must be made in
instruments approved by the
Japanese Bank. Hua Hsing bank-
notes were quoted at $1.55 as
against the Chinese National dollar.
Face Uncertainties
"No one can tell what the rate
is going to be tomorrow," comment-
ed the businessman. "Consequent-
ly, no one can determine what the
cost of his imports will be when
they actually reach China from
foreign countries."
He pointed out that until the
ruling went into effect, foreign
businessmen here, aided by the gold
unit system of the Customs, could
calculate far in advance what the
value of their imports would be in
terms of the Chinese National dol-
lar.
Under the present arrangement
he said, the value of the Chinese
dollar is subject to the whims
of the puppet banks and the
Japanese from day to day."
The uncertainties which will
inevitably prevail over the local
foreign business community, he
stated will be the least of the
evils of the new Customs ruling.
He asserted that the ultimate re-
sult would be the complete exclu-
sion of foreign business in Shang-
hai.
Existing Condition
"It is true foreign business in
Shanghai and elsewhere has suffer-
ed since the decline of the value of
the Chinese dollar," he went on,
"but traders can still obtain for-
eign currency in the market with-
out restriction. And in some
cases, they can even obtain ex-
change at the Chinese Government
rate."
Once the Hua Hsing banknotes
become the general medium of ex-
change, businessmen will find it
impossible to obtain foreign ex-
change unless they get the written
consent of the Japanese Govern-
ment.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》
1939年9月2日
24458
新海关
规定引发
不确定性

据称最终结果将是
对外贸易被彻底
排挤

华兴钞票
投入使用

预见获取
外汇之困难

上海的洋商生意注定要完蛋。
一位知名商人在接受《大美晚报》采访时做出了这一预测，当时他被要求评论上海江海关的新规定，该规定要求以华兴银行钞票支付关税、捐税及费用。
日本人昨日实施了该规定，他们以33名横滨正金银行的职员替换了作为关税征收处雇员的中国银行职员。当征收处在一片混乱中于昨晨开门时，大楼周围贴出了海报，规定100元及以上的付款必须使用经日本银行批准的票据。华兴钞票对中华民国国币的报价为1.55比1。
面临不确定性
“没人知道明天的汇率会是多少，”这位商人评论道。“因此，没人能确定他们的进口货物从国外实际抵达中国时的成本是多少。”
他指出，在该规定生效之前，这里的外国商人在海关金单位制度的帮助下，可以提前很久计算出其进口货物以中华民国国币计值的价值。
他说，在目前的安排下，国币的价值日复一日地受制于傀儡银行和日本人的 whims（一时兴致/任意妄为）。
他表示，当地外国商界不可避免地普遍存在的不确定性，将是新海关规定带来的诸多弊端中最轻的一个。他断言，最终结果将是外国商业在上海被彻底排挤。
现状
“的确，自国币价值下跌以来，上海及其他地方的外国商业遭受了损失，”他继续说道，“但商人仍可在市场上不受限制地获得外汇。在某些情况下，他们甚至能以中国政府规定的汇率获得外汇。”
一旦华兴银行钞票成为通用的交换媒介，商人将发现除非获得日本政府的书面同意，否则不可能获得外汇。

pages.en:
24459

Commenting on Hua Hsing notes
a currency the businessman
stated that it had "barely reached
that status. The puppet bank
has so far issued only $2,600,000
worth of notes for area being
sufficient even for Shanghai cir-
culation.
And you don't call a money a
currency until it has become in
general use," he added. The pre-
sent circulation of Chinese national
dollars in Shanghai totals $300,-
000,000.

Receipts Diminish

In the opinion of the informant,
the Japanese have resorted to the
new Customs measure as a result
of fast diminishing returns from
Customs receipts at present. He
revealed that even as early as last
July, Japanese authorities had pro-
posed the enforce the new ruling
but their proposal was promptly
turned down by financial quarters
in Tokyo who were still in fear
that foreign interests, hard hit by
the scheme, would take retaliatory
measures.
Incomes from the Customs dur-
ing the first six months of 1939, he
indicated, reached roughly a total
of $72,000,000. Deposited in the
Yokohama Specie Bank, this
amount was said to have yielded
approximately £2,400,000 to the
Japanese when the value of the
Chinese dollar averaged 6d
throughout the period.
With the diminishing value of
the Chinese dollar, and declines in
foreign trade, it was added, the
Customs receipts for the next six
months naturally will also diminish.
Observers believed total Custom in-
come for the next six months will
not total $48,000,000, yielding ap-
proximately £750,000 to the Japan-
ese at the present rate of exchange.

Aim Of Ruling

"By requiring the payment of
Customs duties, dues and fees in
Hua Hsing notes whose value was
arbitrarily fixed at 1.55, the
Japanese will obtain at least a 55
per cent increase in Customs
receipts for the rest of the year."
The businessman interviewed also
smacked a blow on the allegation
that Hua Hsing banknotes could be
exchanged for foreign currency as
announced by the Japanese and
the bank officials on July 21. The
Hua Hsing banknotes, it was
stated, would be pegged to the
pound sterling at 6d.
"What actually happens," he said,
"is that the Japanese are playing
with the Chinese National dollar.
At the present exchange rate of the
dollar, they can afford to fool the
public. Holders of Hua Hsing
notes invariably obtained them
with national dollars at the rate
prescribed by the bank, that is, as
it was two weeks ago, at the rate
of 1.77."
pages.zh:
24459

在评论华兴钞票时，这位商人指出，这种货币“ barely reached that status（几乎未达到那种地位）。傀儡银行迄今为止仅发行了价值2,600,000元的钞票，甚至不足以供上海流通。
‘除非一种货币被普遍使用，否则你不能称其为通货，’”他补充道。目前上海流通的中华民国国币总额为300,000,000元。

收入减少

据消息人士认为，日本人采取新的海关措施是由于目前关税收入迅速减少。他透露，早在去年7月，日本当局就曾提议实施新规定，但该提议很快被东京金融界驳回，因为他们仍担心受到该计划沉重打击的外国利益集团会采取报复措施。
他指出，1939年前六个月的海关收入总额约为72,000,000元。这笔款项存入横滨正金银行，据说在此期间国币平均价值为6便士，为日本人带来了约2,400,000英镑的收益。
随着国币价值下跌和对外贸易衰退，据补充说，接下来六个月的海关收入自然也会减少。观察家认为，接下来六个月的海关总收入不会达到48,000,000元，按当前汇率计算，将为日本人带来约750,000英镑的收益。

规定的目的

“通过要求以价值被 arbitrarily fixed（任意固定）为1.55的华兴钞票支付关税、捐税及费用，日本人在今年剩余时间里将获得至少55%的海关收入增长。”
受访商人还驳斥了日本人及银行官员于7月21日宣布的华兴银行钞票可兑换外币的说法。据称，华兴银行钞票将以6便士的汇率与英镑挂钩。
“实际情况是，”他说，“日本人是在拿中华民国国币做戏。按目前的美元汇率，他们糊弄公众还付得起代价。华兴钞票持有者 invariably（总是）是按银行规定的汇率用国币获得的，也就是像两周前那样，汇率为1.77。”

pages.en:
24460

Besides he added there
are only H H $2,000,000 in the
market and one cannot buy too
much foreign exchange with that
sum even if he is in possession of
the entire amount.
Text Of Notice
The text of the Yokohama Specie
Bank notice which was posted in
the Customs Collection Office is as
follows:
"The public is hereby informed
that checks are only acceptable by
this bank in case they are cashier's
orders issued by the Japanese
banks Hua Hsing Commercial Bank
or foreign banks or checks certified
by the above banks, made payable
to this bank.
"The payment of duties, dues
and Customs fees for the sum of
more than N.C.$100 is only
received by the checks above-
mentioned."
Despite this ruling, foreign traders
and customs brokers were reported
to have made payments to the Cus-
toms yesterday in Chinese dollars
and even checks issued by Chinese
banks. A large crowd gathered in-
side the Collection Office some of
them having stood there for hours
since the bank clerks were unable
to supply them with Hua Hsing
banknotes.
pages.zh:
24460

此外，他补充说，市场上仅有2,000,000元华兴钞票，即使一个人拥有全部金额，也无法用这笔钱购买太多外汇。
通告全文
张贴在关税征收处的横滨正金银行通告全文如下：
“特此告知公众，本行仅接受由日本银行、华兴商业银行或外国银行开具的本票，或由上述银行保付并指定支付给本行的支票。
“金额超过国币100元的关税、捐税及海关费用的支付，仅接受上述支票。”
尽管有此规定，据报道，外国商人和报关行昨日仍以中国元甚至中国银行开具的支票向海关付款。大量人群聚集在征收处内部，其中一些人已在那里站立数小时，因为银行职员无法向他们提供华兴银行钞票。

pages.en:
24434
SHANGHAI TIMES
SEP 2 1939

Friction Caused By Change
In Customs Collection

Central Bank Of China Collection Office In
Customs Building Taken Over By Japanese
In Order To Enforce New Regulations

Members of the Yokokohama Specie Bank have reportedly replaced the entire staff of the Central Bank of China Customs Collection Office, located in the buildings of the Shanghai Chinese Maritime Customs Administration, since yesterday morning, following the introduction of the use of Hua Hsing Commercial Bank notes for payment of Customs duties, dues and fees, effective as from yesterday.

In reply to an inquiry made at reliable sources yesterday, "The Shanghai Times" was informed that the entire staff of the Central Bank of China Customs Collection Office resigned their posts from 7.30 p.m. on Thursday. Reports that they had voluntarily resigned under instructions from the Ministry of Finance of the Chinese National Government in Chungking, as a protest against the use of Hua Hsing banknotes, lacked official confirmation yesterday.

The new staff members now attached to the Customs Collection Office are reported to be Japanese employees of the Yokohama Specie Bank.

The work of collecting Customs duties, dues and fees was being carried on smoothly yesterday. A large number of Chinese Customs brokers and foreign shipping agents were to be seen complying with the new regulations as issued by order of Mr. Li Chien-nan, Superintendent of the Shanghai Chinese Maritime Customs Administration, an appointee of the Reformed Government.

Notice Posted

A public notice posted by the Yokohama Specie Bank yesterday runs as follows:—
"The public is hereby notified that cheques are only acceptable by

the bank in case they are cashier's orders issued by the Japanese banks, Hua Hsing Commercial Bank, or the foreign banks, or cheques certified by the above banks, made payable to this bank.

"The payment of duties, dues and Customs fees for the sum of more than $100 Shanghai currency is only received by the cheques above-mentioned."

However, it was learnt from competent quarters that cheques made out to payers by the Central Bank of China, the Bank of Communications, the Bank of China and the Farmers' Bank of China are equally acceptable to the Yokohama Specie Bank on behalf of the Customs Collection Office.

Payment with Hua Hsing Bank notes in any amount to meet Customs dues, however, is not placed under any restrictions. The reason given as to why payment with Chinese legal tender should be restricted to $100 each time was that it was designed to save time in counting them.

S. M. P. officers and a posse of Customs preventive police officers were to be seen guarding the approaches to the Customs Collection Office throughout yesterday.

The entire staff of the Central Bank of China attached to the Customs Collection Office has moved back to their business office on Avenue Joffre where they are to be assigned to take up new duties, pending instructions from the head office in Chungking, it was learnt yesterday.

It was understood that a set of new regulations would shortly be issued by the Yokohama Specie Bank on behalf of the Customs Collection Office for the information of the public.

《上海泰晤士报》
1939年9月2日

关税征收变更引发摩擦

位于海关大楼内的中国银行关税征收处
被日方接管以执行新规

据报道，自昨日早晨起，随着使用华兴商业银行钞票支付关税、捐税及费用的规定于昨日生效，横滨正金银行（Yokokohama Specie Bank）的成员已替换了位于上海中国海关税务司署大楼内的中国银行关税征收处的全部职员。

《上海泰晤士报》昨日向可靠消息人士查询后获悉，中国银行关税征收处的全体职员已于周四晚7时30分辞职。有关他们根据重庆国民政府财政部的指示自愿辞职以抗议使用华兴银行钞票的说法，昨日尚未得到官方证实。

据悉，目前隶属于关税征收处的新职员为横滨正金银行的日籍雇员。

昨日的关税、捐税及费用征收工作进行顺利。可以看到大量中国报关行和外国船务代理遵守由维新政府任命的上海中国海关税务司李健南先生下令发布的新规。

张贴告示

横滨正金银行昨日张贴的公共告示内容如下：——
“特此通知公众，本行仅接受由日本银行、华兴商业银行或外国银行开具的本票，或由上述银行保付并指定支付给本行的支票。

“金额超过上海货币100元的关税、捐税及海关费用的缴纳，仅接受上述支票。”

然而，据权威方面获悉，由中国银行、交通银行、中国银行及中国农民银行开给付款人的支票，横滨正金银行代表关税征收处同样予以接受。

然而，使用任何金额的华兴银行钞票缴纳海关捐税不受任何限制。关于为何限制每次使用中国法币支付的金额为100元，给出的理由是为了节省点钞时间。

昨日全天，均可看到上海公共租界工部局警务处（S. M. P.）警员及一队海关缉私警察守卫在关税征收处的入口附近。

据悉，隶属于关税征收处的中国银行全体职员已搬回霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）的营业办公处，等待重庆总行的指示，以便分配新的任务。

据了解，横滨正金银行将代表关税征收处不久发布一套新规，以供公众知晓。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
SEP 2 1939
24467

Japanese Take Over Central
Bank Customs Offices

New Regulations in Force Since Yesterday : Export
Duties Remain Unaffected ; Precautions Taken

THE Yokohama Specie Bank has taken over offices of the
Central Bank of China in the Customs House. This occurred
yesterday morning after the employees of the Chinese Govern-
ment institution had no other alternative but to leave, following
the new Customs regulations in force since yesterday morning,
according to which Hwa Hsing bank-notes at the rate of 6d
would henceforth be demanded for the purchase of Customs Gold
Units and that Chinese legal tender would be accepted only at
the actual market rate. This would have forced the Central
Bank of China to deal in currency which is not recognized by the
Chungking Government and would have deprived them of their
privilege of fixing the collection rate which in future will be
done by the Superintendant of Customs.

Two notices were posted in the
offices yesterday afternoon. In the
first one the public was informed
that cheques are only acceptable if
issued by Japanese or foreign bank
or the Hwa Hsing Bank, or if certified
good for payment by these institu-
tions. Furthermore, all cheques
would in future have to be made
payable to the Yokohama Specie
Bank. Standard dollars, the notice
further stated, would only be accept-
able up to a maximum amount of
$100. The second notice fixed the
office hours as ending at 3 p.m. daily
which will cause considerable difficul-
ties for exporters as hitherto it was
possible to pay export duties up to
6 and 7 p.m.

It was understood, however, from
reliable sources that this difficulty
would soon be removed although no
official statement to this effect was
available yesterday.

The new regulations will cause an
increase in import duties of about 55
per cent. while export duties will
remain unchanged for the time being
and will be payable in Chinese Na-
tional dollars as in the past. Customs
brokers interviewed yesterday said
that the new regulations did not
actually mean a large increase in
some commodities as compared to the
duties in force up to June of last year,
when, it will be recalled, new tariffs
were enforced, reducing the duty pay-
able for certain commodities consider-
ably, while others were increased.

Accounts Liquidated Earlier

Very few persons were seen paying
customs duty yesterday as most
Shanghai businessmen had liquidated
all their customs accounts in the last
few days of August when it became
known that the new regulations
would be enforced as from yesterday.
Considerable speculation prevailed
in business circles here yesterday as
to whether Duty Orders issued by
the Central Bank of China before
yesterday would be recognized and
accepted by the new organization and,
while no definite information was
available on the subject, it was held
likely that this would be the case.

Meanwhile, members of the River
Police were stationed at all doors to
the office in question, while a large
number of Chinese and Indian con-
stables of the Shanghai Municipal
Police were on duty at the various
entrances to the Customs House.

Rumours were current yesterday
that the Japanese were also contem-
plating the taking over of the Shang-
hai General Post Office but this was
strongly denied by Post Office
officials questioned on the subject
yesterday.

《字林西报》
1939年9月2日
24467

日方接管中国银行
海关办事处

新规自昨日生效：出口关税不受影响；已采取预防措施

横滨正金银行已接管海关大楼内中国银行的办事处。据称，此事发生于昨日早晨，在该中国政府机构雇员别无选择只能离开之后，原因是自昨日早晨起生效的新海关规定，即今后购买海关金单位需按6便士的汇率使用华兴银行钞票，且中国法币仅按实际市场汇率接受。这将迫使中国银行处理一种不被重庆政府认可的货币，并将剥夺其确定征收汇率的特权，该特权今后将由海关税务司行使。

昨日下午在办事处张贴了两份告示。第一份告示通知公众，仅当支票由日本或外国银行或华兴银行开具，或由这些机构认证保证支付时，方可被接受。此外，今后所有支票必须指定支付给横滨正金银行。告示还指出，标准银元仅在接受最高限额100元以内。第二份告示规定办公时间每日至下午3时结束，这将给出口商带来相当大的困难，因为此前支付出口关税的时间可至下午6点和7点。

然而，据可靠消息来源了解，这一困难很快将被消除，尽管昨日尚无就此发表的官方声明。

新规将导致进口关税增加约55%，而出口关税暂时保持不变，并像过去一样以中国国币支付。昨日受访的报关行表示，与去年6月生效的关税相比，新规实际上并不意味着某些商品的大幅增加。回想起来，当时实施了新税则，大幅降低了某些商品的应缴关税，而其他商品则有所增加。

提前结清账目

昨日很少见到有人缴纳关税，因为大多数上海商人在8月的最后几天得知新规将从昨日起生效后，已结清了所有海关账目。昨日商界普遍猜测，中国银行在昨日之前签发的关税缴款书是否会被新机构承认和接受，虽然对此没有确切消息，但人们认为很可能会被接受。

与此同时，水上警察成员驻守在该办事处的所有门口，而大量上海公共租界工部局警务处的华捕和印捕在海关大楼的各个入口处执勤。

昨日有谣言称，日本人也在考虑接管上海邮政总局，但昨日就此询问的邮局官员强烈否认了这一说法。

1939年9月2日

华兴银行

据该银行昨日发布的声明，截至8月31日，流通中的华兴商业银行钞票及辅币分别为1,233,339元和15,556.30元，总计1,248,895.30元。
这些数字显示，与8月15日公布的数据相比，钞票减少了161,359元，辅币减少了3,331.20元。
减少的原因归结为：与前一个月相比，没有未偿还的出口货物贷款，以及与维新政府账户相关的大额支付。
随着周五起开始使用华兴钞票支付关税，以及秋季收购蚕茧季节的临近，预计流通中的钞票数量将会增加。

No. S.
Date

Standard and other local newspapers :- 1939 (F ^)

MORE JAPANESE EMPLOYEES FOR THE CUSTOMS

The Japanese are again spreading reports about an increase in the Japanese staff of the Shanghai Maritime Customs. Enquiries made of the senior Chinese staff of the Customs show that it is generally believed that the increase will not materialize because a number of foreign and Chinese Customs officers are still idle through restraint, as for instance in the case of the crew of the Customs cruisers. As a matter of fact the Customs is at present over-staffed. If it is necessary to increase the staff, all idle officers should first be given something to do. The Commissioner of Customs will not agree to an increase in the already large Japanese staff. It is said that, if necessary, the Chinese staff, who are all men of good character, have decided not to remain at their posts.

编号 S.
日期

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：- 1939 (F ^)

海关增加更多日籍雇员

日本人再次散布关于上海江海关日籍职员增加的消息。向海关高级华员查询后显示，人们普遍认为这一增加不会实现，因为许多外籍和华籍海关官员仍因受制约而闲置，例如海关巡舰船员的情况就是如此。事实上，海关目前人员过剩。如果确有必要增加人手，应首先给所有闲置官员安排工作。海关税务司不会同意增加已经庞大的日籍职员队伍。据说，如有必要，品行端正的华籍职员已决定不留在岗位上。

Standard :-

CUSTOMS ADMINISTRATION STILL INTACT

The fate of the administration of the Shanghai
Maritime Customs is causing much concern among Chinese and
foreigners. Many strange reports are rife about the
transfer of Customs revenues to the Yokohama Specie Bank.
According to information secured by our
reporter, the request made by the Japanese to the Shanghai
Maritime Customs for more Japanese employees shows that
the Japanese have an imperfect knowledge of the
administration of the Customs. The authority to
engage or dismiss men is vested with the Office of the
Inspector-General of the Customs, and if the Japanese
have any demands to make, they should forward same to
that office and not to the Shanghai Maritime Customs.
As a matter of fact, the various departments of the
Shanghai Maritime Customs cannot engage more men of any
nationality whatever.

《字林西报》：-

海关行政机构依然完整

上海江海关行政机构的命运引起了中外人士的极大关注。关于将关税收入转移至横滨正金银行的奇怪谣言四处流传。
据本报记者获得的消息，日本人向上海江海关要求增加更多日籍雇员，这表明日本人对海关行政管理了解不全。聘用或解雇人员的权力属于海关总税务司署，如果日本人有此要求，应向该署提出，而不是向上海江海关提出。事实上，上海江海关各部门无法增聘任何国籍的更多人员。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 1217
Date ____ / ____ / 39

January 17, 1939. Morning Translation.

China Evening News of Jan. 16s

JAPANESE REFUSE TO HAND OVER CUSTOMS REVENUE FOR
REPAYMENT OF FOREIGN LOANS

The following information was secured this morning by our reporter from reliable sources:-
Following the conclusion of an Anglo-Japanese Customs Pact on May 3, 1938, the revenue of the Shanghai Maritime Customs was deposited with the Yokohama Specie Bank instead of with the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. Up to the present about $20,000,000 are on deposit with the Yokohama Specie Bank and as the Shanghai Maritime Customs has no more surplus revenues, the entire amount is used to repay foreign loans. However, the Japanese recently refused to hand out the revenue deposited with the Yokohama Specie Bank for the repayment of foreign loans on the following pretexts: (1) That the Chinese Government has not agreed to refund the Japanese Boxer Indemnity, and (2) That another ¥20,000,000 of revenue, which had been deposited with the Shanghai and Hongkong Banking Corporation, has not been transferred to the Yokohama Specie Bank.
The provisional Customs pact concluded by Britain and Japan on May 3, 1938, is simply a measure to ensure the repayment of foreign loans from the revenue of the Chinese Customs in the occupied areas. No consent to this agreement had been secured from the National Government and a spokesman of the Chinese Government has pointed out that the two points presented by the Japanese are merely pretexts. This has surprised Britain for she has evidently been duped again by Japan. In the meantime, France and America, particularly the latter, are indignant over Japan's disregard of their interests.
The transfer of Customs revenues to the Yokohama Specie Bank was made through the Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China, because the revenue is still being handed to the Central Bank of China which deposits same with the Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China which will be held responsible for this huge amount, but under the present circumstances, it is impossible to reach a settlement. However, the local Chinese community holds the view that since she has been duped, Britain should cease depositing Customs revenue with the Yokohama Specie Bank. Such a step will be most advantageous to the interests of Britain, America and other third Powers.
The Ministry of Finance of the National Government has drawn up measures to deal with this question and has issued an order that in future no more overdrafts from the Central Bank of China to refund those foreign loans secured on the Customs revenues will be passed, but as regards other foreign loans which are to be repaid by Customs revenues outside the war zones, China, in order to preserve her credit, will continue to repay the loans. If the revenue of the Customs in the war zones is paid to the Inspector-General of the Customs as usual, then normal conditions for the repayment of foreign loans will be restored. This statement is warmly supported by the people in Shanghai and is regarded as a wise measure to stabilize the economic system.

1939年1月17日。晨间译文。

1月16日《中国晚报》

日本拒绝移交用于偿还外债的海关收入

本报记者今晨从可靠来源获得以下信息：-
继1938年5月3日英日海关协定签订后，上海江海关的收入存入横滨正金银行，而非汇丰银行。截至目前，约有2,000万美元存入横滨正金银行，由于上海江海关不再有盈余收入，全部款项均用于偿还外债。然而，日本人最近以以下借口拒绝交出存入横滨正金银行用于偿还外债的收入：(1) 中国政府未同意退还日本庚子赔款；(2) 另有2,000万日元收入此前存入上海汇丰银行，尚未转移至横滨正金银行。
英国和日本于1938年5月3日签订的临时海关协定，仅仅是一项确保从被占领区的中国海关收入中偿还外债的措施。国民政府并未同意该协定，中国政府发言人指出，日本提出的两点仅仅是借口。这令英国感到惊讶，因为她显然再次被日本欺骗。与此同时，法国和美国，尤其是后者，对日本无视其利益感到愤怒。
海关收入通过印度新金山中国汇理银行转移至横滨正金银行，因为收入仍移交给中央银行，中央银行将其存入印度新金山中国汇理银行，该行将对这笔巨额款项负责，但在目前情况下，不可能达成结算。然而，当地华人社区认为，既然英国已被欺骗，她应停止将海关收入存入横滨正金银行。此举将最有利于英国、美国及其他第三国的利益。
国民政府财政部已制定措施处理此问题，并发布命令，今后不再通过中央银行透支来偿还那些以海关收入为担保的外债，但对于其他由战区以外海关收入偿还的外债，中国为维护其信用，将继续偿还贷款。如果战区的海关收入像往常一样支付给海关总税务司，那么偿还外债的正常条件将得到恢复。这一声明受到上海民众的热烈支持，并被视为稳定经济体系的明智之举。

SHANGHAI TIMES

JAN 17 1939

Japanese
Spokesman
On Funds

Why Money Held In The
Yokohama Specie Bank
Is Not Released

Execution in full by the Chinese
Maritime Customs of the terms
stipulated in the Anglo-Japanese
agreement of May 3, 1938, is a pre-
requisite for a possible servicing of
loans secured on Customs revenue
cut of funds now being held in
deposit by the Yokohama Specie
Bank, a Japanese Embassy spokes-
man said yesterday evening.

"I am not in a position to discuss
a hypothetical question, but it would
seem to me that the terms of the
agreement should be carried out
first before that question is raised,"
he said.

The spokesman emphasized that
these were his personal views. "I
am not aware of discussions on the
matter which may have been taking
place on the subject between Japan-
ese and British officials concerned in
Tokyo, and consequently I am not
in a position to formulate an opin-
ion," he said.

"It seems to me, however, that an
agreement is concluded with a view
to carrying out its terms," he added.

Chungking's Failure

The Japanese authorities, it was
recalled, refused to carry out their
part of the agreement following the
failure of the Chungking régime to
agree to the execution of some por-
tions of the accord.

Remaining unexecuted are the
agreement to transfer to the Yoko-
hama Specie Bank the balance of
the Customs accounts with the
Hongkong and Shanghai Bank in
each port under Japanese occupation
and the undertaking to pay to the
Japanese Government arrears of the
Japanese portion of the Boxer In-
demnity held at the Hongkong and
Shanghai Bank since September
1937.

Julia
C.Y.

《字林西报》

1939年1月17日

日本
发言人
谈资金

为何存于
横滨正金银行
的资金未被释放

日本大使馆发言人昨晚表示，完全执行1938年5月3日英日协定中规定的条款，是可能利用目前存于横滨正金银行的资金来偿付以海关收入为担保的贷款的先决条件。

“我无权讨论假设性问题，但在我看来，在提出该问题之前，应先执行协定的条款，”他说。

该发言人强调，这些是他的个人观点。“我不知道东京相关的日本和英国官员之间是否正在就此问题进行讨论，因此我无权形成意见，”他说。

“不过，在我看来，签订协定是为了执行其条款，”他补充道。

重庆方面的失败

回顾起来，由于重庆政权未能同意执行协定的部分内容，日本当局拒绝履行其协定中的部分义务。

尚未执行的内容包括：将各被日军占领港口在汇丰银行的海关账户余额转移至横滨正金银行的协议，以及向日本政府支付自1937年9月以来存放在汇丰银行的日本庚子赔款欠款的承诺。

Julia
C.Y.

海关表格将使用日语

日本邮船会社官员开始执行程序

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN 1 5 1939

Present Position Regarding
Chinese Customs Revenue

Japanese Embassy Spokesman Says Halting Of
Service On Loans Due To Non-Co-operation
By Chungking; Funds In Local Banks

Failure of the Chungking regime to agree to the execution of some portions of the An lo-Japanese agreement regarding the Chinese Maritime Customs, concluded on May 3 last year, was blamed yesterday evening by a Japanese Embassy spokesman for the continued halting of service on various loans secured on the Customs revenue.

The unexecuted provisions of the accord, he said, included, among others, the agreement to transfer to the Yokohama Specie Bank the balance of the Custom accounts with the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank in each port under Japanese occupation, and the promise to pay to the Japanese Government arrears of the Japanese portion of the Boxer Indemnity, held at the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank since September, 1937.

All Customs revenue collected in Shanghai since the conclusion of the agreement was being held in deposit by the Yokohama Specie Bank under the terms of the Anglo-Japanese agreement.

With the exception of a withdrawal of $1,000,000 in June for the service on the Reorganization Loan of 1913, the entire sum was being left untouched, he said.

The Reformed Government, the spokesman declared, had received neither an advance from these funds, nor had floated a loan with Customs revenue as security.

The spokesman declined to disclose the amount now being held in deposit by the Yokohama Specie Bank on the grounds that he understood that the local Customs authorities did not wish to have the figure revealed.

Asked what steps were being taken with regard to the interests of the United States, France and other Powers in loans secured on Customs revenue, the spokesman referred his questioners to the text of a communique issued in London and in Tokyo on May 3, 1938.

The communique stated: "It is further understood that the Governments of the United States and France do not propose to raise any objection to the temporary application of these arrangements, which will be subject to reconsideration in the event of a radical change occurring in economic conditions."

Amount Unrevealed

Asked if it was correct that the amount now deposited in the Yokohama Specie Bank was about $25,000,000, the spokesman said that he had no information as to the amount.

"Are negotiations now going on in one way or another or are things just stagnant now?" asked a correspondent. He was told that the situation could not remain in its present position for ever.

Asked how it was that the Reorganization Loan of 1913 came to be serviced, but none of the others, the Embassy spokesman said that he thought it was probably because that was the first loan to come up for service. Later, the servicing of loans was discontinued.

（批：File R 1/1）
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》。
1939年1月15日

关于中国海关税收的当前状况

日本大使馆发言人称，由于重庆方面不合作，导致以关税为担保的贷款偿付工作停止；资金存于当地银行

日本大使馆发言人昨晚指责重庆政权未能同意执行去年5月3日达成的安乐-日本协定（An lo-Japanese agreement）中有关中国海关的部分条款，这是导致以关税收入为担保的各项贷款继续停止偿付的原因。

他说，该协定中未执行的条款包括：同意将日军占领下各口岸汇丰银行（Hongkong and Shanghai Bank）海关账户的余额转至横滨正金银行（Yokohama Specie Bank），以及承诺支付自1937年9月以来存放在汇丰银行的庚子赔款中属于日本部分的欠款。

根据英日协定的条款，自该协定达成以来在上海征收的所有海关收入，均由横滨正金银行代为保管。

他说，除了去年6月提取了100万美元用于偿付1913年善后借款（Reorganization Loan）外，其余款项均未动用。

该发言人宣称，维新政府（Reformed Government）既未从这些资金中获得预付款，也未以海关收入为担保发行过贷款。

发言人拒绝透露目前由横滨正金银行保管的金额，理由是他获悉当地海关当局不希望公开这一数字。

当被问及针对美国、法国及其他列强在以关税为担保的贷款中的利益正在采取何种措施时，该发言人请提问者参阅1938年5月3日在伦敦和东京发布的公报文本。

该公报称：“此外还谅解，美国和法国政府不打算对这些安排的临时适用提出任何异议，若经济状况发生根本性变化，则将重新审议。”

金额未披露

当被问及目前存入横滨正金银行的金额是否约为2,500万美元时，发言人表示他对此金额没有信息。

“现在是否正在进行某种形式的谈判，还是局势处于停滞状态？”一名记者问道。他得到的答复是，目前的状况不可能永远持续下去。

当被问及为何1913年善后借款得到了偿付，而其他借款却没有时，大使馆发言人表示，他认为这可能是因为该笔借款是首笔到期需偿付的借款。随后，贷款偿付工作便停止了。

（批注：档案 R 1/1）

CHINA PRESS.

JAN 1 5 1939

Customs Funds To
Be Frozen Pending
New Developments

Japanese Claim British Stipulations In 1937
Agreement Not Carried Out By Chungking;
Transfer Of Old Revenue Demanded

SPOKESMAN REFUSES TO DIVULGE AMOUNT
TAKEN IN SINCE NIPPONESE OCCUPATION

Because China has refused to recognize the Anglo-Japanese Shang-
hai Customs "agreement" of 1937, and has "failed to carry out sti-
pulations made by Great Britain" in the pact, Customs funds collected
in Shanghai will be held by the Yokohama Specie Bank so long as
the present situation exists, it was announced at the Japanese press
conference last night by the Embassy spokesman.

Terms of the 1937 "agreement,"
declared the spokesman, had been
published in London and Tokyo last
year, and he was unable to discuss
matters which had not been pub-
lished at that time. He also stated
that it was indicated by Great Bri-
tain at the time that other nations
interested in China loans had raised
no objection to the agreement.

Among the stipulations made by
Great Britain in the "agreement,"
said the spokesman, was a condi-
tion that funds collected by the
Customs prior to the Japanese oc-
cupation should be transferred to
the Inspector-General, Sir Frederick
Maze. This had not been done.

**1913 Loan Serviced**

"Following the enforcement of
the Anglo-Japanese 'agreement' of
1937 on May 3, last year," the Em-
bassy spokesman announced, "all
collections made by the Shanghai
Customs and the Customs in Jap-
anese-occupied territory were de-
posited with the Yokohama Specie
Bank.

"Just over a million dollars were
paid out of these funds last year to
service the China Reorganization
Loan of 1913, but as a result of the
Chinese Government's failure to
carry out certain stipulations made
by Great Britain in the 'agreement,'
no further payments have been
made."

The spokesman said that he had
no information as to how much had
been deposited by the Chinese Mari-
time Customs with the Shanghai
and Hongkong Bank prior to the
"agreement," nor could he divulge
the amount which had been de-
posited with the Yokohama Specie
Bank since the Japanese occupation.

**Not Given To Puppets**

"The 'Reformed Government' has
neither received any of these funds,
nor have they been used by the
'Reformed Government' as security
for loans," continued the spokes-
man.

"According to my information," a
foreign correspondent commented,
"the United States Government took
no part in this 'agreement,' and
they did not agree to anything.
What about other nations? What
becomes of their loans?"

Other interested nations had no
objections to the "agreement" when
it was made, replied the spokesman.
According to comment made in
London at the time the "agree-
ment" was made, the United States
did agree, he continued.

Pressed for further information
on this point, the spokesman de-
clared that he preferred not to
discuss details of the "agreement"
which had not been made public
in London or Tokyo.

**Money Held In Bank**

"My question has nothing to do
with the agreement," pursued the
correspondent. "I want to know
whether any loans are being ser-
viced from funds now being held
by the Shanghai and Hongkong
Bank. Is this money being held,
or is it not? When will any loans
be serviced?"

Replying that the money was
being held by the Yokohama Specie
Bank, the spokesman said he be-
lieved that no further payments
would be made "so long as the
present situation existed." "This
situation might remain forever, as
things go," he added.

pondent, "the Great Britain's loans

1939年1月15日

海关资金将被冻结
以待新进展

日方声称重庆方面未履行
1937年协定中的英国规定；
要求移交旧有收入

发言人拒绝透露
自日军占领以来收取的金额

日本大使馆发言人在昨晚的新闻发布会上宣布，由于中国拒绝承认1937年的英日上海海关“协定”，并“未能履行”该协定中“英国作出的规定”，只要目前局势存在，在上海征收的海关资金将由横滨正金银行保管。

发言人宣称，1937年“协定”的条款已于去年在伦敦和东京公布，他无法讨论当时未公布的事项。他还表示，英国当时指出，其他关注中国贷款的国家对这一协定并未提出异议。

发言人说，英国在“协定”中作出的规定之一是一项条件，即日军占领前由海关征收的资金应移交给总税务司梅乐和爵士（Sir Frederick Maze）。这一点尚未做到。

**1913年借款已获偿付**

大使馆发言人宣布：“自去年5月3日实施1937年英日‘协定’以来，上海海关及日军占领区海关征收的所有款项均存入横滨正金银行。

“去年从这些资金中支付了略超过100万美元，用于偿付1913年中国善后借款，但由于中国政府未能履行‘协定’中英国作出的某些规定，此后未再进行任何支付。”

发言人表示，他不知道在“协定”签订之前中国海关在上海汇丰银行存放了多少资金，也无法透露自日军占领以来存入横滨正金银行的金额。

**未交给傀儡政权**

发言人继续说道：“‘维新政府’既未收到这些资金中的任何一部分，也未将这些资金用作‘维新政府’贷款的担保。”

一名外国记者评论道：“据我所知，美国政府并未参与这一‘协定’，也没有同意任何事项。其他国家呢？它们的贷款怎么办？”

发言人回答说，在达成“协定”时，其他相关国家并未提出异议。他接着说，根据当时在伦敦发表的评论，美国确实表示了同意。

当被要求就此点提供更多信息时，发言人宣称，他不愿讨论未在伦敦或东京公开的“协定”细节。

**资金存于银行**

该记者追问：“我的问题与协定无关。我想知道，目前是否有贷款正从上海汇丰银行持有的资金中获得偿付。这笔钱是被扣留了，还是没有？何时会有贷款获得偿付？”

发言人回答说，资金正由横滨正金银行持有，并表示他认为“只要目前局势存在”，就不会再进行任何支付。“照此情形，这种局势可能会永远持续下去，”他补充道。

**美国“被冷落”**

该记者说：“在我看来，英国的贷款是由上海汇丰银行持有的资金作为担保，

而日本的贷款是由横滨正金银行持有的资金作为担保。美国和其他国家却被冷落在一旁？”

随后，发言人承认，横滨正金银行持有的海关资金将被“冻结”，直到局势改变且出现更有利的进展允许其释放为止。

“这是否意味着日本的贷款利益也未得到偿付？”——有人问发言人。他给予了肯定的回答。

“为何单独挑出1913年善后借款进行偿付？”——另一名记者问道。发言人说，这是因为该笔借款是“协定”达成后首笔到期需偿付的借款。

“协定”未获承认

众所周知，英国政府最近否认其未正式采纳1937年英日“协定”。这一否认是在致日本外务省的一份照会中作出的。

美国也已表明，它不接受在日军占领区实施的新关税税率的合法性。

日方要求

据昨日日本媒体报道，上海海关官员与日本邮船会社（N.Y.K. Steamship）官员之间的谈判，已就进口申报单使用日语的问题达成了友好解决。

鉴于日本在进口列表中居首位，日本邮船会社坚持认为，就海关程序的便利和便捷而言，日本进口商应获得与其他列强国民相同的待遇。据悉，经过谈判，该公司已签发日文提单。他们还准备立即签发发票。其他日本公司和进口公司也被鼓励效仿日本邮船会社的做法。

据报道，日本驻上海总领事馆官员已与海关当局完成谈判，将在海关高级职位中安插相当数量的日本人，这标志着简化日本进口程序的又一步骤。《大陆新报》（Tairiku Shimpo）昨日报道，拟任的日本官员人选已由日本领事馆选定。一家海关分支机构计划不久将在一个尚未确定的地点开设。

CHINA PRESS.
JAN 1 3 1939
Nippon Daily
Urges Custom
House Reform

Says Japanese Should
Be Permitted In
Documents

ASKS HIGH POSTS
FOR NIPPONESE

Sees Bright Future For
Trade Of Island
Empire

Immediate reforms in the Shanghai Maritime Customs are being urged by Japanese merchants and traders here, according to the Finance and Business Section of the Tai-riku Shimpo yesterday.
Contending that import declarations should be permitted to be filed out in the Japanese language, as well as Chinese and English, as practiced in North China ports, and insisting that some of the higher posts in the Shanghai Customs should be held by Japanese, Japanese business leaders have made representations to the Customs authorities, the daily reported.
Written protests over the signature of Mr. Masaji Yoshida, President of Japanese Chamber of Commerce and Industry, have been forwarded to the puppet "Reformed Government," the Shanghai Maritime Customs, and Japanese authorities concerned asking that official steps be taken to speed up the needed improvements, the daily said.

Claims Supported
Warm support was given the demands for reform in the editorial columns of the same newspaper yesterday. "Discriminatory measures" against Japanese trade as enforced previously should be done away with immediately, the paper declared, as Japanese trade is now on top of the import list.
Since the establishment of the "Reformed Government," most of the "evils" practiced against Japanese commerce, as well as in other fields of Japanese activity in China, have been "eradicated," the editorial asserted. With a bright future in prospect for Japanese trade in China, two problems have still to be solved.

Delays Alleged
Complicated import procedure has caused the loss of commercial opportunities among Japanese merchants, while merchandise is menaced with damage and decomposition because of the delay. These handicaps also are responsible for mounting storage fees against Japanese importers, the daily commented.
The proposal to appoint Japanese officials to some of the high posts should "not be construed as a Japanese attempt to secure special privileges," the paper pointed out, but is "intended only to secure a smooth functioning of import procedure," the editorial concluded.

（右上角批注：REGISTRY S. R. D.）
（右侧手写批注：G 13/1）

1939年1月13日
《日本日报》
敦促海关改革

称应允许在文件中使用日语

要求给予日本人高级职位

看好岛帝国贸易的光明前景

据昨日《大陆新报》财经版报道，在沪日本商人及贸易商正敦促对上海海关进行即时改革。

该日报报道，日本商界领袖已向海关当局提出交涉，主张进口申报单应允许像华北港口那样，除中文和英文外也可用日语填写，并坚持上海海关的一些高级职位应由日本人担任。

该日报称，以日本工商会议所会长吉田正次（Masaji Yoshida）先生署名的书面抗议书已递交给傀儡“维新政府”、上海海关及相关日本当局，要求采取官方步骤加速进行必要的改进。

诉求获得支持

昨日，同一家报纸的社论栏对改革要求给予了热烈支持。该报宣称，鉴于日本贸易目前在进口列表中居首位，应立即废除此前实施的针对日本贸易的“歧视性措施”。

社论断言，自“维新政府”成立以来，针对日本商业以及在中国其他领域日本活动的绝大多数“弊病”已被“根除”。随着日本对华贸易前景光明，仍有两个问题有待解决。

声称存在延误

该日报评论道，复杂的进口程序导致日本商人丧失商业机会，而货物因延误面临损坏和腐烂的风险。这些障碍也导致日本进口商的仓储费用不断攀升。

该报指出，任命日本官员担任部分高级职位的建议“不应被解释为日本试图获取特权”，社论总结称，其“旨在仅确保进口程序的顺畅运行”。

（右上角批注：登记处 S. R. D.）
（右侧手写批注：G 13/1）
（右侧盖章/手写字：档案）

"JAPANESE ENGAGED IN IMPORT BUSINESS DEMAND SHANGHAI
CUSTOMS TO ENGAGE JAPANESE FOR HIGH POSITIONS
AND THE IMPORT APPLICATION FORM BE PRINTED
IN JAPANESE LANGUAGE"

On December 6, 1938 the Shanghai
Japanese Chamber of Commerce, in the name of Mr. Yoshida,
Chairman, sent a letter to the "Reformed Government", the
Customs and the Japanese authorities to increase the
number of custom officers and to exhibit more efficiency
in the examination of imported goods.
The gist of the letter is as
follows:- "Since the 'Reformed Government' has taken over
the Customs, reforms being gradually introduced to improve
Sino-Japanese co-operation. As a result Japanese products
have gained a wider market, showing a return of business.
Thus the situation has turned favourable for Sino-Japanese
economic co-operation. However, the Customs procedure
relating to imported goods requires many days to complete
and in the worst case it requires about 20 days. As a
result of the procedure, importers are losing business
opportunities and are obliged to pay godown charges as
they are not allowed to keep imported goods in the
Customs godown for more than 10 days after discharge
from the ship. In addition, the goods are liable to
sustain damage, become rotten or lose weight causing
considerable loss to the importers.
The above trouble is due to the
following causes:-
1. Delay in examination of goods because of a shortage
of Custom officers.
2. Inefficient examination due to insufficient
experience on the part of the Custom officers.
In order to improve the situation
a more simple procedure must be adopted.
A section of importers has
proposed the following procedures:-
1. The import application forms used in Central
China are printed in English and Chinese but not in
Japanese and the form used here is more complicated than
that used in North China. The import application form
here should be printed in Japanese language also as is
being done in the North, considering the quantity of
Japanese goods imported.
2. The applications are handled by the recording
department of the Customs, but no Japanese holds a high
post in that department. This has given rise to much delay.
More Japanese should be engaged for high positions in
the Customs.

N. . . D ____ ISTRY

TERIKU
SH . . P.

“从事进口业务的日方要求上海海关聘用日本人担任高级职位，并将进口申请表印成日文”

1938年12月6日，上海日本商工会议所以主席吉田（Yoshida）先生的名义，向“维新政府”、海关及日本当局致函，要求增加海关职员人数，并提高进口货物查验效率。
该函要点如下：“自‘维新政府’接管海关以来，逐步推行改革以改善中日合作。结果，日本产品获得了更广阔的市场，显示出商业复苏的迹象。因此，局势已转向有利于中日经济合作。然而，与进口货物相关的海关手续需耗时多日才能完成，最坏情况下约需20天。由于这些手续，进口商失去了商业机会，并被迫支付仓库费用，因为他们不被允许在货物卸船后将进口货物存放在海关仓库超过10天。此外，货物容易受损、腐烂或失重，给进口商造成相当大的损失。
上述麻烦是由于以下原因造成的：
1. 因海关职员短缺，导致货物查验延误。
2. 因海关职员经验不足，导致查验效率低下。
为了改善这一状况，必须采用更简便的手续。
部分进口商提出了以下建议：
1. 华中地区使用的进口申请表仅印有英文和中文，未印日文，且此处使用的表格比华北地区使用的更为复杂。考虑到日本进口货物的数量，此处的进口申请表也应像华北那样加印日文。
2. 申请由海关记录部门处理，但该部门没有日本人担任高级职务。这造成了许多延误。海关应聘用更多日本人担任高级职位。

December 25, 1938. Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News and other local newspapers (24-12)

JAPAN TO RAISE CHINESE CUSTOMS TARIFF.

In an attempt to boycott British and American
trade in North China and as a reprisal against the action
of the British and the American Governments in granting
loans to China, the Japanese authorities have instigated
the Peiping Provisional Government to raise the Customs
tariff on British and American goods in North China.
On December 23 a reporter of this paper called
on certain subordinates of Sir Frederick Maze, Inspector-
General of Chinese Maritime Customs, and was given the
following information:-
"The Inspector-General will never approve or
recognize such tariff changes. Owing to control by the
special influence, the administration of various Custom
Houses in North China has already been impaired. In
case the tariff is raised, the importation of British and
American goods into North China will be seriously affected
and the various Powers will raise an opposition."
Foreign merchants in Shanghai are also paying
close attention to this matter as they are fully aware that
Japan is attempting to monopolize China's market and to drive
away the interests of third Powers. They hope that their
respective Governments will unite and exert pressure upon
Japan.

1938年12月25日。晨间译件

《中美日报》及其他本地报纸（12月24日）

日本拟提高中国关税。

为了抵制英美在华北的贸易，并作为对英美政府向中国提供贷款行为的报复，日本当局唆使北平临时政府提高英美货物在华北的海关关税。
12月23日，本报记者拜访了中国海关总税务司梅乐和爵士（Sir Frederick Maze）的某些下属，获悉以下信息：
“总税务司绝不会批准或承认此类关税变更。由于受到特殊势力的控制，华北各海关的管理已经受到损害。如果提高关税，英美货物进入华北的进口将受到严重影响，列强也将提出反对。”
在上海的外国商人也密切关注此事，因为他们充分意识到日本正试图垄断中国市场并排挤第三国的利益。他们希望各自政府联合起来，向日本施加压力。

December 28, 1938. Afternoon Translation

Standard and other local newspapers :-

POWERS AND THE REVISED CUSTOMS TARIFF

The attempt of the Japanese and the puppet regime to overthrow the trade of Britain, America and other third Powers with China and the reported changes in the Customs tariffs in North China as from January 1 have attracted considerable attention among the British, American and French authorities and merchants in Shanghai.

According to information secured from reliable sources, Sir Archibald Clark Kerr, the British Ambassador to China, who is now in Shanghai, is maintaining close touch with Sir Frederick Maze, Inspector-General of the Customs, and is closely watching the situation. The local American Consulate-General is also constantly seeking information from the Customs regarding the importation and dumping of Japanese goods as well as the raising of the Customs tariff in North China.

Sir Frederick Maze has declared that his consent had not been sought in connection with the compulsory alterations in the Customs tariff in North China. Sir Frederick added that he will never recognize the increased tariff for about 90 items, most of which affect British and American goods.

1938年12月28日。午后译件

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

列强与修订后的海关关税

日本及傀儡政权试图推翻英国、美国及其他第三国与中国的贸易，以及据报道自1月1日起华北海关关税发生变更，这一情况引起了在上海的英国、美国和法国当局及商人的极大关注。

据从可靠渠道获得的消息，目前身处上海的英国驻华大使阿奇博尔德·克拉克·卡尔爵士（Sir Archibald Clark Kerr）正与海关总税务司梅乐和爵士（Sir Frederick Maze）保持密切联系，并密切关注局势。美国驻沪总领事馆也不断向海关寻求有关日本货物进口及倾销以及华北海关关税提高的信息。

梅乐和爵士声明，关于华北海关关税的强制性变更，并未征求他的同意。梅乐和爵士补充说，他绝不会承认针对约90种商品增加的关税，其中大多数影响英美货物。

December 18, 1938. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE CUSTOMS NOT VIOLATED

It would be interesting to learn whether the administration of the Shanghai Maritime Customs has been violated. Recently it was reported that several alterations in the Customs tariff have taken place. It was also said that a Japanese spokesman has publicly declared that the administration of the Customs is taking orders from the Ministry of Finance of the "Reformed Government".

On December 17, our reporter called on a certain high Chinese employee of the Customs, who made the following statement :- "It is a fact that the administration of the Customs has not been violated. Although the Customs has been subjected to oppression since the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from Shanghai, no changes have been made in the administration and all its affairs are being carried out in accordance with the orders issued by the National Government. It is undeniable that on occasions the Customs has experienced much difficulty in the execution of its duties. Tariffs have been changed but this was only in districts where the Customs cannot exercise its authority. The report that the Customs had accepted orders from the Ministry of Finance of the "Reformed Government" is entirely groundless."

1938年12月18日。晨间译件。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

海关行政未受侵犯

了解上海江海关的行政是否受到侵犯将是很有意思的。最近有报道称海关关税发生了几次变更。还有人说，一位日本发言人公开宣称，海关行政正在接受“维新政府”财政部的命令。

12月17日，本报记者拜访了海关的一位中国高级雇员，他发表了如下声明：“海关行政未受侵犯是事实。虽然自中国军队撤离上海以来，海关一直遭受压迫，但行政管理并未发生变化，其所有事务均按照国民政府发布的命令进行。不可否认，海关在执行职责时偶尔会遇到很大困难。关税确实发生了变更，但这仅发生在海关无法行使权力的地区。关于海关接受‘维新政府’财政部命令的报道完全毫无根据。”
