CHINA PRESS.

DEC 1 5 1938

Lawford Said
“Instructed”
By Nanking

Customs Head Receives
Order From ‘Reformed
Gov’t’—Spokesman

COMMISSIONER HAS
“NOTHING TO SAY”

Spokesman Promises To
Investigate Complaint
On Export Duties

“You must ask Mr. Lawford for this information,” replied a spokesman of the Japanese Embassy at a Press conference yesterday afternoon when he was asked for information concerning alterations alleged to have been made recently in the local Customs tariff schedule.

“Where does Mr. Lawford get his orders from,” asked another correspondent. “From the Finance Ministry of the Reformed Government,” replied the spokesman.

A lengthy discussion arose from the original question, and for some time the Embassy spokesman was bombarded with a series of questions regarding reported impositions of taxes previously unannounced.

Fur Coat Taxed

A correspondent informed the Embassy spokesman that some question had arisen over the export from Shanghai of a fur coat. A few days before the coat was dispatched to America, it had been stated, said the correspondent, that no export duty would be levied. When the coat was eventually dispatched, however, an export duty was charged.

Further inquiry at the Customs offices in Shanghai, continued the correspondent, had elicited the information from a Customs official that changes in tariffs were being made so often by the Japanese authorities that the Customs officials themselves “were unable to keep pace with them.”

“They Are Lying”

“That is impossible. They are lying,” interrupted the Embassy spokesman.

The Embassy spokesman said that he would try to obtain a complete copy of the present Customs schedule for the benefit of the Conference, but in the meantime he was not in a position to state whether any changes had been made in the tariff since its publication last spring.

“It was,” declared the spokesman, “customary when tariff rates were changed, for those changes to be made public; in view of the fact that the Japanese authorities are not aware of any changes having been made, it may be assumed that none have been made.”

Inquiry Promised

Questioned regarding the imposition of taxes outside of the Customs schedule, the Embassy spokesman said that nobody other than the Customs were authorized to impose duties on merchandise. He said he would inquire into reported instances in which taxes had been collected by other “authorities,” and agreed to a suggestion that a complete survey of the situation should be made.

Questioned last night regarding the Japanese suggestion that he took his orders from the “Reformed Government Finance Ministry” in Nanking, Mr. Lawford, Commissioner of Shanghai Customs, said that he had no comment to offer on the statement.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》。

1938年12月15日

劳福德称
奉南京方面
“指示”

海关负责人收到
“维新政府”
命令——发言人

专员
“无可奉告”

发言人承诺调查
关于出口税的投诉

“你们必须向劳福德先生询问此信息，”昨天下午在一次新闻发布会上，当被问及据称近期本地海关税则表发生的变更时，日本大使馆发言人回答道。

“劳福德先生从哪里接受命令？”另一位记者问道。“来自维新政府财政部，”发言人回答。

由此引发了长时间的讨论，使馆发言人在一段时间内遭到一系列关于据报道征收此前未宣布的税收的问题轰炸。

皮草大衣被征税

一位记者告知使馆发言人，关于一件皮草大衣从上海出口出现了一些问题。记者称，在大衣发往美国前几天，曾被告知不征收出口税。然而，当大衣最终发出时，却收取了出口税。

记者继续说道，在上海海关办公室的进一步查询从一位海关官员那里得知，日本当局如此频繁地变更关税，以至于海关官员自己“都跟不上变化”。

“他们在撒谎”

“那是不可能的。他们在撒谎，”使馆发言人打断道。

使馆发言人表示，他将尝试获取现行海关税则表的完整副本以供会议参考，但与此同时，他无法说明自去年春季公布以来税则是否有任何变更。

发言人宣称：“惯例是，当关税税率变更时，这些变更会予以公布；鉴于日本当局不知晓有任何变更发生，可以假定没有发生任何变更。”

承诺调查

当被问及在海关税则之外征税的问题时，使馆发言人表示，除海关外，无人有权对商品征收税款。他说，他将调查有关其他“当局”收税的报告案例，并同意对局势进行全面调查的建议。

昨晚，当被问及日本方面暗示他接受南京“维新政府财政部”的命令时，上海海关税务司劳福德先生（Mr. Lawford）表示，他对该声明无可奉告。

November 22, 1938. Afternoon Translation

News Digest :-

**〔此处转录不清〕** OVER THE CUSTOMS

To the workers in the Western District and to the comrades
of a certain party:
We are greatly honoured at having been asked
by you about the hoisting of a five-barred flag over the
Customs and why we have not stirred up a revolt. On behalf
of all Chinese officers and workers in the Customs, I would
like to reply to your question.
The success of our recent struggle was due to
the fact that all the Chinese staff were living in the Customs
Superintendent's Office, so that we had a better chance
to be unified; furthermore, we had at that time several
fearless leaders. These men have since been transferred
to South China. Later on, all the other enthusiastic
elements of the cause were also sent away. The remaining
few enthusiasts continued to struggle but they lacked
experience. From now on we shall start a struggle against
the hoisting of the five-barred flag, and at the same time,
we like to have your advice for we hope to re-establish the
integrity of the Customs and to avenge the insult caused by
the hoisting of the flag.

1938年11月22日。午后译件

《新闻摘要》：

**〔此处转录不清〕** 关于海关

致西区工人及某党同志：
承蒙你们询问关于海关悬挂五色旗一事，以及我们为何未发动起义，我们深感荣幸。我代表海关全体中国职员和工人，回答你们的问题。
我们近期斗争的成功归功于所有中国职员都住在海关监督公署内，从而使我们有更好的机会团结一致；此外，当时我们有几位无畏的领导人。这些人后来已被调往华南。随后，其他热衷于该事业的人员也被调离。剩下的少数热心人士继续斗争，但他们缺乏经验。从现在起，我们将开始反对悬挂五色旗的斗争，同时，我们希望得到你们的建议，因为我们希望恢复海关的廉洁，并为悬挂旗帜所造成的侮辱报仇。

November 22, 1938. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

FIVE-BARRED FLAG OVER THE CUSTOMS BUILDING

The Customs authorities have failed to adopt effective measures in connection with the hoisting of the five-barred flag over the Customs Building. According to reliable information secured from a certain foreign source, the Japanese authorities had first notified Mr. Maze, Inspector-General of Customs, that the five-barred flag would be hoisted and compelled him to change the flag on the basis of the Anglo-Japanese Customs Agreement concluded at Tokyo this spring. This agreement is a temporary measure to deal with the situation during wartime. The transfer of the Customs revenue to the Yokohama Specie Bank was stipulated by this agreement. Mr. Maze flatly refused the demand that the Customs flag be changed, but eventually he had to accept it in view of the conditions to-day.

As the change of the Customs flag is a violation of the Customs administration, the public are highly indignant over the attitude adopted by Mr. Maze; his action must be rectified. Greater care should be exercised over the diplomatic measures to be taken.

The Japanese authorities are dissatisfied with the attitude of Li Chien-nan (李建南), Superintendent of the Shanghai Maritime Customs. The "Reformed Government" has discharged him and appointed Nyi Dao-yuen (倪道元), younger brother of Nyi Dao-long (倪道烺), Governor of Anhwei, to succeed him.

Nyi Dao-yuen accepted the appointment a few days ago at the New Asia Hotel, Hongkew.

1938年11月22日。晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

海关大楼悬挂五色旗

海关当局未能就海关大楼悬挂五色旗一事采取有效措施。据从某外籍人士处获得的可靠消息，日本当局首先通知海关总税务司梅乐和先生，将悬挂五色旗，并强迫他根据今年春天在东京签订的《英日海关协定》更换旗帜。该协定是应对战时局势的临时措施。该协定规定将海关税款移交横滨正金银行。梅乐和先生断然拒绝更换海关旗帜的要求，但鉴于目前的形势，他最终不得不接受。

由于更换海关旗帜违反了海关行政，公众对梅乐和先生所采取的态度极为愤慨；必须纠正他的行为。在将要采取的外交措施上应更加谨慎。

日本当局对上海江海关税务司李建南（Li Chien-nan）的态度不满。“维新政府”已将其免职，并任命安徽省主席倪道烺（Nyi Dao-long）的弟弟倪道元（Nyi Dao-yuen）继任。

倪道元日前在虹口新亚酒店接受了任命。

November 21, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Morning Leader and other local newspapers:

THE HOISTING OF THE FIVE-BARRED FLAG OVER THE CUSTOMS

Yesterday being Sunday, a five-barred flag was again hoisted over the building of the Shanghai Maritime Customs. As Mr. Lawford has failed to deal with the matter, the public are much dissatisfied with him.
According to information secured by our reporter, Japanese river policemen and men in plain clothes have been on duty day and night on the roof of the Customs building since November 4. Customs officers of other nationalities are prohibited from going to the roof. The five-barred flag is hoisted under armed protection and serious trouble will occur should the Customs authorities attempt to stop it. In order to avoid trouble, Mr. Lawford has not made any explanation to the public and it is not known what steps he will take.
The Customs employees are watching developments in the case and will take effective action for the sake of the country.

1938年11月21日。下午译件。

《晨报》及其他本地报纸：

海关悬挂五色旗

昨日为星期日，上海海关大楼再次悬挂五色旗。由于乐华德（Lawford）先生未能处理此事，公众对他甚为不满。
据本报记者获得的消息，自11月4日以来，日本水上警察及便衣人员日夜在海关大楼屋顶执勤。其他国籍的海关职员被禁止登上屋顶。五色旗是在武装保护下悬挂的，如果海关当局试图阻止，将会发生严重事端。为了避免麻烦，乐华德先生未向公众作出任何解释，也不清楚他将采取何种措施。
海关华员正在关注事态发展，并将为国家利益采取有效行动。

November 18, 1938.                                Afternoon Translation

News Digest :-

        THE HOISTING OF A FIVE-BARRED FLAG OVER THE CUSTOMS

    To all Chinese Officers of the Customs:
                    Your fortitude in promoting the campaign for
the protection of the Customs has resulted in a guarantee
being given by the Customs authorities that no bogus flag
will be hoisted over the Customs.
                    On November 4, a five-barred flag appeared
over the Customs building.   This may be regarded as a
warning to England and America to cease dreaming about an
open door policy.
                    We hope that you will continue your struggle.
We shall support you.   We also hope that England and
America will take effective measures instead of lodging
protests.
                                    "All workers of a certain institute
                                     in Western Districts"

    To all Chinese Officers of the Customs:
                    The hoisting of the five-barred flag over the
Customs building has aroused great indignation among the
Chinese people.   We shall support you in the fight with
the Japanese robbers who are planning to take over the
Customs.   It is also a threat to England, America and
France.
                                    "The male and female workers of ---"

    To the Editor,
                    The integrity of the Customs has already been
violated since the signing of the Anglo-Japanese Agreement
in May this year.   Furthermore, a five-barred flag has been
hoisted twice over the Customs building.   I herewith suggest
the dismantling of the flag pole for the time being.
                                    Pung-liu (彭流); a reader.

        海关悬挂五色旗

    致海关全体华员：

November 19, 1938. Morning Translation.

News Digest publishes the following letters:

THE HOISTING OF A FIVE-BARRED FLAG OVER THE CUSTOMS

To all Chinese officers of the Customs:
On November 4, a five-barred flag appeared over the Customs building; on November 13 it was hoisted again. We were greatly excited upon learning of this.
In May this year, you started a campaign for the protection of the Customs. Although this campaign has had no satisfactory result, yet it has prevented the Japanese and the puppet authorities from hoisting the five-barred flag whenever they wished and has preserved a part of the integrity of the Customs. Your struggle has won the respect of the Chinese people throughout Shanghai and other parts of China as well as the sympathy of the whole world.
The people of Great Britain, America and France now fully understand that the Japanese have closed the door to them and unless they render us positive assistance, these powers will not be able to protect their interests in China.
Brave Customs officers! The hoisting of the five-barred flag over the Customs building is not only an insult to the integrity of the Customs, but also a threat to the 4,500,000 Chinese in this "isolated" Shanghai. No doubt you all became indignant at having to work under the five-barred flag. With your glorious past, you should start a "big wave". We shall support you.
(Editor's note: Signed by 81 persons)

Ts Ying Yeh Pao published the following letter on Nov. 16:

To English small friends:
Are you aware that a five-barred flag has been hoisted over the Shanghai Customs House? Our hearts are filled with indignation. The passive attitude of England in this matter fills us with misgivings for Japan has indicated her intention to occupy China and to overthrow all the foreign Powers in China. Japan has thus challenged England.
To write to the English Officers of the Customs is useless and we hope that you will apply sanctions against the public enemy.

FILE
pages.zh:
1938年11月19日。上午译件。

《新闻摘要》刊登以下信件：

海关悬挂五色旗

致海关全体华员：
11月4日，海关大楼出现了一面五色旗；11月13日又再次悬挂。得知此事，我们深感激愤。
今年五月，你们发起了护关运动。虽然该运动未取得令人满意的结果，但它防止了日本人和伪政权随心所欲地悬挂五色旗，并保全了海关的部分完整性。你们的斗争赢得了上海及中国其他地区全体中国人的尊重，以及全世界的同情。
英、美、法三国人民现在充分认识到，日本人已向他们关闭了大门，除非他们给予我们积极的援助，否则这些列强将无法保护其在华利益。
勇敢的海关职员们！在海关大楼悬挂五色旗，不仅是对海关完整性的侮辱，也是对这“孤岛”上海450万中国人的威胁。毫无疑问，你们对在五色旗下工作都感到愤慨。凭借你们光荣的过去，你们应该掀起一场“大浪潮”。我们将支持你们。
（编者注：81人签名）

《中英晚报》于11月16日刊登以下信件：

致英国小朋友：
你们是否知道上海海关已悬挂五色旗？我们心中充满愤慨。英国在此事上的被动态度令我们深感忧虑，因为日本已表明其占领中国并推翻所有在华外国列强的意图。日本 thus 挑战了英国。
写信给海关英籍职员是无用的，我们希望你们对公敌实施制裁。

归档

pages.en:
Chinese-American Daily News :-

Superintendent of Customs to be Changed

At the beginning of this year, the "Reformed
Government" appointed Li Chien-nan ( 李健南 ) as
Superintendent of the Shanghai Maritime Customs. After
taking over the post, Li made many attempts to interfere
with the administration of the Customs, but without success.
Both the Japanese and the puppet authorities are much
dissatisfied with him.
At a joint conference held by the "Reformed
Government" and the Provisional Government at Nanking some
time ago, Wong Keh-min ( 王克敏 ) attacked Li Chien-nan
strongly and suggested to General Doihara that a new
Superintendent of the Shanghai Customs be appointed.
General Doihara agreed with the suggestion.
It is learned that Nyi Dao-yuen ( 倪道遠 ), younger
brother of Nyi Dao-long ( 倪道烺 ), Governor of Anhwei
of the "Reformed Government", will be appointed as new
Superintendent of the Shanghai Maritime Customs. Nyi
Dao-yuen is a member of the former Peiping Clique and is
very much liked by the Japanese.
pages.zh:
《中美日报》：-

海关税务司将更迭

今年年初，“维新政府”任命李健南（Li Chien-nan）为上海海关税务司。李上任后，多次试图干涉海关行政，但未获成功。日本人和伪政权都对他甚为不满。
不久前，“维新政府”与南京临时政府举行联席会议，王克敏（Wong Keh-min）强烈抨击李健南，并向土肥原将军（General Doihara）建议任命新的上海海关税务司。
土肥原将军同意了该建议。
据悉，“维新政府”安徽省长倪道烺（Nyi Dao-long）之弟倪道遠（Nyi Dao-yuen）将被任命为新的上海海关税务司。倪道遠是前北平派系成员，深受日本人喜爱。

pages.en:
Standard and other local newspapers :-

FOREIGN CUSTOMS OFFICERS DISSATISFIED WITH THE
HOISTING OF FIVE-BARRED FLAG OVER CUSTOMS

Local public bodies and residents are indignant
over the continuous hoisting of the five-barred flag over
the Customs building. They have issued a manifesto in
the hope that the Customs employees will explain the
situation. Mr. Lawford has stated that the change of
flag had not been done by the Customs itself. The public,
however, are dissatisfied with the statement.
The Chinese employees of the Customs the
other day sent a joint telegram to Dr. H.H. Kung,
President of the Executive Yuan of the National Government
at Chungking, asking for information. A reply has
reached Shanghai from Dr. Kung, containing directions as

to the attitude the Chinese employees should adopt in
future.
Besides some 100 employees of a certain party,
foreign employees of the Customs are dissatisfied with
the change of flag.
pages.zh:
《标准报》及其他本地报纸：-

外籍海关职员对海关悬挂五色旗表示不满

本地公共团体和居民对海关大楼持续悬挂五色旗感到愤慨。他们发表宣言，希望海关职员说明情况。乐华德先生表示，换旗并非由海关方面所为。然而，公众对该声明表示不满。
日前，海关华员联名致电重庆国民政府行政院院长孔祥熙博士，询问情况。孔博士的回电已抵达上海，其中包含关于华员今后应采取之态度的指示。

除某党派约100名职员外，海关外籍职员也对换旗表示不满。

pages.en:
Morning Leader publishes the following article written by one
Tseng Wan ( 振聞 ):

THE HOISTING OF THE FIVE-BARRED FLAG OVER THE CUSTOMS

With reference to the hoisting of the five-
barred flag over the Customs House, Mr. Lawford, the
Commissioner of the Customs, has lodged protests with the
Japanese Consul-General, whereupon the latter states that
this was done by the authorities of the "Reformed Government"
and has nothing to do with the Japanese authorities.
The Customs House belongs to China and is
of an international nature. It is to be noted that Shanghai
has fallen, but not the Foreign Settlements. Furthermore,
as she is closely connected with the Customs, Great Britain
should take the responsibility of protecting the Customs.
The hoisting of the five-barred flag insults not only China
but also the various Powers concerned, especially Great
Britain. For this reason, the last named should have no
hesitation in tearing down the five-barred flag.
pages.zh:
《晨报》刊登一篇由振闻（Tseng Wan）撰写的文章：

海关悬挂五色旗

关于海关悬挂五色旗一事，海关税务司乐华德先生已向日本总领事提出抗议，后者称此举系“维新政府”当局所为，与日本当局无关。
海关属于中国，且具有国际性质。值得注意的是，上海虽已沦陷，但租界并未沦陷。此外，鉴于英国与海关关系密切，英国应承担保护海关的责任。悬挂五色旗不仅侮辱中国，也侮辱各有关列强，尤其是英国。因此，英国应毫不犹豫地撤下五色旗。

pages.en:
November 15, 1938.                                    Morning Translation.

Morning Leader and other local newspapers :-

        PUBLIC BODIES PETITION GOVERNMENT REGARDING CUSTOMS
                            FLAG ISSUE

                Explaining the hoisting of the five-barred
flag over the Custom House on November 4, the Customs
authorities stated that the flag was hoisted stealthily by
the Japanese and puppet authorities.  On November 6 the
flag was again hoisted.  The Customs observed November 12,
the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, as a holiday, but
did not fly the national flag.  On Sunday, November 13,
the five-barred flag re-appeared over the Custom House.
All this would indicate that the hoisting of the five-barred
flag had not been done stealthily.
                Highly indignant over the affair, important
local public bodies have sent the following telegram to
the Executive Yuan of the National Governments:-
                "The public is irritated by the repeated
hoisting of the five-barred flag over the Custom
House.  This is not only harmful to our national
rights, but is also contrary to agreement.  You are
requested to order the Director-General of Customs
to cease the practice so as to preserve our national
rights and to avert misunderstanding."
                At a secret meeting held the other day by
senior Chinese officials of the Customs, it was resolved
that all Chinese employees should obey the orders of the
Government and not submit to other influence.  As reticence
on the part of the Chinese employees might be mistaken for
reconciliation with the Japanese and puppet authorities, it
was decided that a strong stand be taken and that the
Chinese employees should rather withdraw than work under the
five-barred flag.  The Chinese employees, however, will not
resort to any rash action in view of existing conditions.
pages.zh:
1938年11月15日。                                    上午译件。

《晨报》及其他本地报纸：-

        公共团体就海关旗帜问题向政府请愿

                针对11月4日海关悬挂五色旗一事，海关当局
称该旗是日本人和伪政权暗中悬挂的。11月6日，该
旗再次悬挂。海关将11月12日已故孙中山博士诞辰定
为假日，但未悬挂国旗。11月13日星期日，五色旗再
次出现在海关大楼。这一切表明，悬挂五色旗并非暗
中进行。
                本地重要公共团体对此事深感愤慨，已向国
民政府行政院发送如下电报：-
                “公众对海关反复悬挂五色旗感到激怒。这
不仅损害我国国权，亦违背协定。请饬令海关总
税务司停止此举，以维护我国国权并避免误解。”
                在日前举行的海关高级华员秘密会议上，决
议全体华员应服从政府命令，不受其他势力影响。鉴
于华员的沉默可能被误认为与日本人和伪政权和解，
会议决定采取强硬立场，华员宁可辞职也不在五色旗
下工作。然而，鉴于现有局势，华员不会采取任何鲁
莽行动。

November 14, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Morning Leader and other local newspapers:

THE BOGUS FLAG AGAIN HOISTED OVER THE CUSTOMS BUILDING
ON NOVEMBER 13

After the changing of the flag over the Customs
Building on November 4, it was decided that the bogus
five-barred flag be hoisted on Sundays and anniversary
days of the "Reformed Government". The "Reformed
Government" is said to have received an understanding from
the Customs regarding this measure. It cannot be regarded
as a breach of integrity on the part of the administration
of the Customs.
On November 12, the birthday of the late Dr. Sun
Yat-sen, no flag was hoisted. On Sunday, November 13, a
five-barred flag was hoisted again over the Customs House.
The Chinese employees are greatly angered. They have
held a meeting and will take some action to give expression
to their opinions.

Morning Leader (Editorial):

A five-barred flag was hoisted over the Customs
House again yesterday. Last week when the same flag was
hoisted over the building, the Customs authorities gave the
excuse that it was put there secretly. How can anyone
hoist a flag on top of the Customs building without the
authorities' knowledge? What is Mr. Lawford, the
Commissioner of Customs, doing? How is it that people
have been repeatedly allowed to hoist the flag "secretly"?
The affair has aroused the anger of Chinese
Customs officers and all the residents of Shanghai and has
caused them to doubt the responsible British officials of
the Customs. We quite sympathize with them. The
responsibility of the occurrence is attributable not only to
the British Customs officials, but also to the present
British policy.
Mr. Lawford is a British subject in the employ
of the Chinese Government. Whether he has previous
knowledge or not (in the present case he certainly had),
he should be held responsible for any occurrence that is
detrimental to the integrity of China's administrative
rights. It is not likely that Japan will dare to act
rashly without having secured the understanding of Britain.
From the toleration of Japan's tactics, it can be seen that
there must be some understanding between Japan and Britain.
It may be the opinion of the British Customs
officials that so long as the Customs can carry on its work,
its administration can be considered intact. This is wrong.
The Customs is a part of the Government and it cannot remain
intact while disobeying the orders of the Government.
Some shortsighted British people think that by
making concessions to Japan in regard to the Customs, they
will, in return, be allowed to navigate the Yangtse. This
is a dream. So much has been said about Japan's intention
to drive British and American influences out of China that
we do not think more words necessary. British and American
capitalists will have no part in China unless they are
willing to put their capitals at the disposal of the
Japanese. If Britain, the U.S.A. and other countries
want to protect their interests in China, they must firmly
oppose Japan's policy of plunder. The question of the
Customs is a realistic starting point.
pages.zh:
1938年11月14日。下午译件。

《晨报》及其他本地报纸：

11月13日海关大楼再次升起伪旗

继11月4日海关大楼更换旗帜之后，当局决定在星期日及“维新政府”纪念日悬挂伪五色旗。据悉，“维新政府”已就此事与海关方面达成谅解。此举不应被视为海关行政方面有违诚信。
11月12日乃孙中山先生逝世周年诞辰，当日未悬挂任何旗帜。然而，在11月13日（星期日），海关大楼上再次升起了五色旗。中国职员对此极为愤慨。他们已举行会议，并将采取某些行动以表达其意见。

《晨报》（社论）：

昨日，海关大楼上再次升起了一面五色旗。上周当同一面旗帜在该大楼上升起时，海关当局借口称是有人秘密悬挂的。若未经当局知晓，任何人怎能在海关大楼顶部悬挂旗帜？税务司乐斐德（Lawford）先生正在做什么？为何一再允许人们“秘密”悬挂旗帜？
此事激起了中国海关官员及上海全体居民的愤怒，并致使他们怀疑海关中负有责任的英国官员。我们对此深表同情。此次事件的责任不仅在于英国海关官员，也在于当前英国的政策。
乐斐德先生是受雇于中国政府的一名英国臣民。无论他是否事先知情（在本案中他显然知情），对于任何损害中国行政权完整性的事件，他都应承担责任。日本在未获得英国谅解的情况下，不太可能敢贸然行事。从对日本策略的容忍来看，英日之间必然存在某种谅解。
英国海关官员或许认为，只要海关能继续开展工作，其行政管理便可视为完好无损。这是错误的。海关是政府的一部分，在违背政府命令的同时，不可能保持其完整性。
一些目光短浅的英国人认为，通过在海关问题上对日本做出让步，作为回报，他们将获准在长江航行。这简直是痴人说梦。关于日本意图将英美势力驱逐出中国的言论已不胜枚举，我们认为无需多言。除非英美资本家愿意将其资本交由日本支配，否则他们在中国将无立足之地。如果英国、美国及其他国家希望保护其在华利益，就必须坚决反对日本的掠夺政策。海关问题是一个现实的切入点。

News Digest publishes the following letters :-

The Change of Flag of the Shanghai Customs

To the entire body of Chinese employees of the Shanghai
Maritime Customs :
On November 4, we saw a bogus flag fly over
the building of the Shanghai Maritime Customs. This
pre-arranged action on the part of the Japanese authorities
constitutes an insult not only to the Chinese people
throughout the country but also to Great Britain, America,
France and other Powers. Japan has impaired China's
Customs administration and violated the interests and
positions of the Powers in China. We must co-operate
with Britain, America and France and deal her a serious
blow.
You have a glorious history in the past and
we hope that you will launch a more brave struggle with
an undaunted spirit. Have a clear understanding of
our only army and be consolidated for a great struggle!
Chinese residents in Shanghai will give you powerful
support.
From a group of young students.
The letter was signed by Loo Poo-n (鲁波文),
Ler Lei-ts (雷履之), Tsi Chung-lo (季仲乐) and others.
----------

Editor :
On the morning of November 9, when we learned
from newspapers that Mr. Lawford and the employees of
the Customs were entirely loyal to the National Government,
we ran to our classroom and shouted: "Little friends!
Stand up! Give a salute to Mr. Lawford who supports
justice and the employees of the Customs who are loyal
to the National Government!"
At once, all the little friends stood up.
Why have such determined and patriotic children; can he
not conduct us?
We have to advise teachers of primary schools
in Shanghai not to relax their efforts, but to lead
children to support struggles that are loyal to our
fatherland.

Chan Hao-i (陈豪义), Siro Ching
(小清), Chang Sz-yee (张思义),
Wong Ying (王英) and five other
teachers of a primary school.

《新闻摘要》刊登以下信件：

上海海关换旗事件

致上海海关全体中国职员：
11月4日，我们看到一面伪旗在上海海关大楼上空飘扬。日本当局这一预谋行动，不仅是对全中国人民的侮辱，也是对英国、美国、法国及其他列强的侮辱。日本破坏了中国的海关行政，侵犯了列强在华的利益和地位。我们必须与英、美、法合作，给予其沉重打击。
你们过去有着光荣的历史，我们希望你们以大无畏的精神发起更勇敢的斗争。清楚认识我们唯一的军队，并为伟大的斗争而团结起来！上海中国居民将给予你们强有力的支持。
一群青年学生敬上
此信由鲁波文（Loo Poo-n）、雷履之（Ler Lei-ts）、季仲乐（Tsi Chung-lo）等人署名。
---

编辑：
11月9日上午，当我们从报纸上得知乐斐德先生及海关职员完全忠于国民政府时，我们跑到教室喊道：“小朋友们！起立！向支持正义的乐斐德先生及忠于国民政府的海关职员致敬！”
立刻，所有小朋友都站了起来。
既然有如此坚定和爱国的孩子，他难道不能引导我们吗？
我们要劝告上海的小学教师不要松懈努力，而要引导儿童支持忠于我们祖国的斗争。

陈豪义（Chan Hao-i）、小清（Siro Ching）、张思义（Chang Sz-yee）、王英（Wong Ying）及另外五位小学教师。

November 11, 1938. Morning Translation.

News Digest publishes the following letters :-

(1)

To the Chinese officers of the Shanghai Customs:
The policy of compromise of Mr. Chamberlain has created an unsatiable desire in the aggressors. The hoisting of a bogus flag over the Customs house is a sign of Japan's plans for aggression. By hoisting this flag, she is trying to coerce the people of Shanghai into submission and to show Britain and the U.S.A. the power of the Imperial Army, thereby warning them against dreaming about open doors or equal rights.
Our brave Customs officers have in the past carried on glorious struggles. Their Customs Protection Movement drew forth the support and respect of people throughout the country. We are in more difficult circumstances than before, but we must preserve our former spirit and struggle without hesitation.
We several hundred working youths are angry at the hoisting of the five-barred flag. We hope our Government, Customs officers and people will unanimously oppose the hoisting of this flag over the Customs House.
We wish to offer the following suggestions to the Customs officers:
(1) All Customs officers should unite without regard to the difference of cliques or past disagreements.
(2) The Customs officers should unite with all public bodies and people in Shanghai.
(3) We must not admit of compromise, but should fight to the end.
We hope that you will execute your duties so as not to disappoint the people.

From a group of working youths.
November 10.

1938年11月11日。上午译件。

《新闻摘要》刊登以下信件：

(1)

致上海海关中国官员：
张伯伦（Chamberlain）先生的妥协政策在侵略者心中造成了无法满足的欲望。在海关大楼悬挂伪旗是日本侵略计划的标志。通过悬挂这面旗帜，她试图胁迫上海人民屈服，并向英美展示皇军的威力，从而警告他们不要妄想门户开放或权利平等。
我们勇敢的海关官员在过去进行了光荣的斗争。他们的护关运动赢得了全国人民的支援和尊敬。我们的处境比以往更加艰难，但我们必须保持以往的精神，毫不犹豫地斗争。
我们数百名劳动青年对悬挂五色旗感到愤怒。我们希望我国政府、海关官员和人民一致反对在海关大楼悬挂这面旗帜。
我们谨向海关官员提出以下建议：
(1) 所有海关官员应团结一致，不计派系差异或过往分歧。
(2) 海关官员应与上海所有公共团体和人民联合。
(3) 我们绝不接受妥协，而应战斗到底。
希望你们履行职责，不负众望。

一群劳动青年敬上
11月10日。

November 9, 1938.
Morning Translation

News Digest and other local newspapers :-

THE AFFAIR OF THE LOCAL CUSTOMS

Mr. Lawford, Commissioner of the Shanghai
Maritime Customs, has denied that the Customs has changed
its flag. Yesterday Mr. Lawford issued an order declaring
November 12, the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, as
a holiday in accordance with the orders of the National
Government. All internal and external affairs of the
Customs will continue to be conducted according to the
orders and wishes of the National Government.
Watch duties in the Customs House have been
taken over by foreign officers who will do their best to
prevent a recurrence of the recent flag incident.

News Digest publishes the following two letters :-

Two Open Letters To Customs Officers

(1) Officers of the Shanghai Maritime Customs:
The incident on November 4 is intolerable.
We are indignant at the shameful act of the Japanese and
their running dogs; at the same time, we respect your
loyalty to the country and your spirit of struggle.
The humiliation is not only intolerable to
the Customs officers who have to pass under the bogus
flag daily, but also to the 4,000,000 residents of
Shanghai.
The vicious Japanese are unsatiable. They
will want to seize other rights once they have seized the
Customs. Therefore by protecting the Customs rights, we
are protecting other rights also and every Chinese should
oppose the changing of the flag by the Customs.
As a result of her policy of compromise,
Great Britain is now being challenged by Japan. We hope
Britain will reconsider her policy.
Customs officers! It is glorious to fight
for the country. Let us die rather than submit to insult.
We are a group of primary school teachers in
Shanghai. We will unite all primary school teachers and
children in Shanghai to support you!
Wishing you victory.
Tai Kwei (戴桂), Wu Wan-tseng (吴琬贞),
Tseng Sung (曾生), Li Ying (李颖),
Tseng Ching (曾静), Kuh Loh-sih (顾乐诗),
Ghui Zung-zai (瞿宗才), Hwa Ching (华菁),
Chow Vung (周文) and Li Ming (黎明).
November 6.

(2) The Brave Chinese Officers of the Customs:
Mr. --- has told us that the shameful five-
barred flag has been hoisted over the Customs House. How
distressing is this! We are waiting to see you take
revenge. We hope you will unite and deal a blow to the
shameless traitors and the Japanese Imperialists.
Brethren, you are our vanguards and we are
your support. We want to see our national flag again.
We want to save China.
From a little friend, Liang Yuan-tao (梁元道).

1938年11月9日。

《新闻摘要》及其他本地报纸：

本地海关事件

上海海关税务司乐斐德先生否认海关已更换旗帜。昨日，乐斐德先生发布命令，宣布根据国民政府的指令，将11月12日孙中山先生逝世周年诞辰定为假日。海关的所有内外事务将继续按照国民政府的命令和意愿办理。
海关大楼的看守职责已由外籍官员接管，他们将尽力防止近期挂旗事件再次发生。

《新闻摘要》刊登以下两封信：

致海关官员的两封公开信

(1) 上海海关官员：
11月4日的事件是不可容忍的。我们对日本人及其走狗的无耻行径感到愤慨；同时，我们尊重你们对国家的忠诚和斗争精神。
这种耻辱不仅对于每日必须从伪旗下经过的海关官员来说是不可容忍的，对于上海四百万居民来说也是如此。
邪恶的日本人贪得无厌。一旦夺取了海关，他们还将企图夺取其他权利。因此，保护海关权利也就是保护其他权利，每个中国人都应反对海关换旗。
由于其妥协政策，英国正受到日本的挑战。我们希望英国重新考虑其政策。
海关官员们！为国争光而战是光荣的。宁死不受辱。
我们是一群上海的小学教师。我们将联合上海所有小学教师和儿童来支持你们！
祝你们胜利。
戴桂（Tai Kwei）、吴琬贞（Wu Wan-tseng）、曾生（Tseng Sung）、李颖（Li Ying）、曾静（Tseng Ching）、顾乐诗（Kuh Loh-sih）、瞿宗才（Ghui Zung-zai）、华菁（Hwa Ching）、周文（Chow Vung）及黎明（Li Ming）。
11月6日。

(2) 勇敢的海关中国官员们：
某先生告诉我们，那面可耻的五色旗已在海关大楼升起。这是多么令人痛心啊！我们等待着看你们复仇。希望你们团结起来，给无耻的汉奸和日本帝国主义者以打击。
兄弟们，你们是先锋，我们是你们的后盾。我们要再次看到我们的国旗。我们要拯救中国。
小朋友，梁元道（Liang Yuan-tao）敬上。

MAI.IC.I

PROBLEM CONCERNING FLYING OF FIVE BARRED
FLAG BY CUSTOMS

The Shanghai Mainichi publishes
th. following leading article under the above headlines:
Following the publication of
an article in this paper which questioned the omission
of the Shanghai Customs to hoist a flag, which had been
donated by a gentleman named Chokoitsujin, the Customs
authorities on November 4 raised the five barred flag at
the mast on top of the Custom House building. On
November 7 the authorities removed the flag. As a
result all anti-Japanese Chinese newspapers in Shanghai
published leading articles condemning the Customs.
The attitude adopted by the
Customs is believed to have been occasioned by an
objection raised by a section of Chinese Custom officers
and the promptings of anti-Japanese Chinese newspapers.
It is, however, a shameful attitude on the part of the
Customs.

As a result of the Anglo-
Japanese agreement, the Shanghai Customs was transferred
to the "Reformed Government" in May this year and the
entire revenue of the Customs is being handed over to
the "Reformed Government". It is believed that all
officers who opposed the transfer have already left the
Customs. If there are still some in opposition the
Customs should discharge them. The Customs should not
worry about opposition from anti-Japanese Chinese newspapers
because these papers only oppose so that they may secure
financial support from the National Government. The
Shanghai Customs should up-hold its respect and dignity.
Chinese residents in Shanghai
call Shanghai an isolated island, but this term can
only be applicable to anti-Japanese elements. It is
painful for us to witness the Customs' attitude regarding
the use of the flag. The "Reformed Government" should
issue an order to the Shanghai Customs to use the five
barred flag permanently.
pages.zh:
MAI.IC.I

关于海关悬挂五色旗的问题

《上海每日新闻》以如上标题刊登了以下社论：
继本报刊登一篇质疑上海海关未悬挂由一位名为 Chokoitsujin 的绅士捐赠的旗帜的文章后，海关当局于11月4日在海关大楼顶部的桅杆上升起了五色旗。11月7日，当局撤下了该旗帜。结果，上海所有反日的中文报纸均发表社论谴责海关。

据信，海关所采取的态度是由于部分中国海关职员提出反对以及反日中文报纸的煽动所致。然而，海关的这种态度是可耻的。

由于英日协定，上海海关于今年5月移交给“维新政府”，海关的全部收入正移交给“维新政府”。据信，所有反对移交的官员已离开海关。如果仍有反对者，海关应将其解职。海关不必担心反日中文报纸的反对，因为这些报纸之所以反对，只是为了从国民政府获得财政支持。上海海关应维护其尊严和体面。

在上海的中国居民称上海为“孤岛”，但这一术语仅适用于反日分子。目睹海关在旗帜使用问题上的态度，令我们感到痛心。“维新政府”应向上海海关发布命令，永久使用五色旗。

Kuo Chi Jih Pao Evening Edition (7/11) and other local newspapers:

"Reformed Government" to Take Over Customs in Occupied
Areas

Chinese employees of the Custom House are
angry at the changing of the flag. They will support the
integrity of the Customs rights.
The changing of the flag by the Customs was not
carried out secretly, but was forced by circumstances. It
is said that the hoisting of the flags over the Custom
House and certain vessels on the Whangpoo was ordered by
the highest official of the local Customs. These
flags are now under the charge of a responsible person, and
will be hoisted every Sunday and anniversary day hereafter.
Having succeeded to a certain extent in taking
over the local Customs House, the "Reformed Government of
the Chinese Republic" is planning to take over the Customs
Houses at Nanking, Hangchow, Chinkiang, Wuhu, Kiukiang,
Canton and other fallen districts. It is said that
arrangements have already been completed. The "Reformed
Government" will first restore the Nanking Custom House
and will transfer men for work there from the existing
staff. Chinese members of the staff at various Custom
Houses, however, are determined not to co-operate with
the "Reformed Government".
pages.zh:
《国字日报》晚刊（11月7日）及其他本地报纸：

“维新政府”将接管占领区海关

海关大楼的中国雇员对更换旗帜感到愤怒。他们将支持海关权利的完整性。

海关更换旗帜并非秘密进行，而是迫于形势。据说，在海关大楼和黄浦江上某些船只上升挂旗帜的命令是由当地海关最高官员下达的。这些旗帜目前由一名负责人保管，此后每逢星期日及纪念日都将悬挂。

“中华民国维新政府”在某种程度上成功接管了当地海关后，正计划接管南京、杭州、镇江、芜湖、九江、广州及其他沦陷地区的海关。据悉，相关安排已经完成。“维新政府”将首先恢复南京海关，并从现有职员中调派人员前往工作。然而，各海关的中国职员决心不与“维新政府”合作。

November 8, 1938.
Morning Translation

China Evening News of November 7 :-

THE FLYING OF FIVE-BARRED FLAGS OVER THE CUSTOMS

On November 6, five-barred flags again appeared over the Customs administration building and the Harbour Office.

Interviewed by a reporter of this paper, a certain foreign Customs officer of the rank of Commissioner declared that the flying of five-barred flags over the Customs building on November 4 and 6 was compulsory. On the first occasion it was done by puppet officials assisted by plain-clothes men of a certain party, while on the second occasion Japanese gendarmes in civilian clothes were present and the man directing the hoisting of the flag was the kidnapper of Yang Wen-loong (楊文龍) and Chang Wen-kwei (張文奎), two revenue guards of the Customs, sometime ago. This man who is still known to some members of the Customs staff can speak English fluently.

According to information given out by Customs employees, the cause of the flying of the strange flags is attributable to the exportation of a quantity of silver on board the s.s. President Coolidge, because the Customs authorities had issued a permit authorizing the exportation. This incurred great displeasure among the Japanese and puppet authorities and Li Chien-nan (李建南), the puppet Superintendent of the Customs, was severely reprimanded. The object of the compulsory flying of strange flags is intended, in the first place, as a demonstration to foreign and Chinese Customs officers and in the second as an act of retribution towards the Customs authorities.

Under the present peculiar circumstances, the Customs authorities are finding it difficult to prevent the hoisting of the flag. However, the entire body of foreign Customs officers are adopting a similar attitude as that of the Chinese staff, that is, they listen only to instructions from the National Government at Chungking. On the morning of November 7, Mr. Lawford, the Commissioner of the Shanghai Maritime Customs, announced his stand to the Chinese and foreign staff, declaring that the strange flags had been hoisted without his consent, that he absolutely refused to recognize a change of flag and that he would accept only the orders of Sir Frederick Maze, the Inspector-General, in the administration of the Shanghai Maritime Customs, while Sir Frederick Maze obeys the instructions of the Ministry of Finance of the National Government.

It is learned that the Chinese staff of the Customs have resolved to adopt the following attitude :-
(1) That for the time being they will continue to work under the guidance of Sir Frederick Maze, the Inspector-General, and Mr. Lawford, the Commissioner of the Customs.
(2) That they will not work for the rebels and will resign en bloc when it becomes no longer worthwhile for them to preserve the Shanghai Maritime Customs.

1938年11月8日。
晨间译稿

11月7日《中国晚报》：

海关悬挂五色旗

11月6日，五色旗再次出现在海关行政大楼和海务处上方。

本报记者采访了一位职级为税务司的外籍海关官员，该官员声明，11月4日和6日在海关大楼悬挂五色旗是强制性的。第一次是由傀儡官员在某党派便衣人员的协助下进行的，而第二次则有便衣日本宪兵在场，指挥升旗的人是前不久绑架两名海关缉私员杨文龙（Yang Wen-loong）和张文奎（Chang Wen-kwei）的绑匪。此人仍为部分海关职员所认识，能讲流利的英语。

据海关雇员提供的消息，悬挂奇异旗帜的原因归咎于“柯立芝总统号”轮船出口大量白银，因为海关当局签发了准许出口的许可证。这引起了日本人和傀儡当局的极大不满，傀儡海关总监李建南（Li Chien-nan）受到严厉斥责。强制悬挂奇异旗帜的目的，首先是为了向中外海关职员示威，其次是对海关当局的报复行为。

在目前特殊的情况下，海关当局发现难以阻止升旗。然而，全体外籍海关职员采取了与中国职员相同的态度，即只听从重庆国民政府的指示。11月7日上午，上海江海关税务司劳福德（Lawford）先生向中国和外籍职员宣布了他的立场，声明悬挂奇异旗帜未经他同意，他绝对拒绝承认更换旗帜，并且在上海江海关的管理上只接受总税务司梅乐和爵士（Sir Frederick Maze）的命令，而梅乐和爵士则服从国民政府财政部的指示。

据悉，海关中国职员已决定采取以下态度：
(1) 暂时继续在总税务司梅乐和爵士和海关税务司劳福德先生的指导下工作。
(2) 不为叛乱分子工作，当维持上海江海关不再值得时，他们将集体辞职。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
NOV 4 1938
Customs Raises
Reformers' Flag
Five-Bar Emblem Seen
On Bund For First
Time In Years

The old five-bar flag of the Chinese Empire and early Republic, now the emblem of the new Japanese - sponsored "Reformed Government," flew from the mast high above the Shanghai Customs House on the Bund this morning for the first time.
It replaced the familiar tricolor of the national government of China, which flew there until the Chinese troops left Shanghai.
The red-yellow-green-white-black flag was raised over the Customs House, the Customs examination house on the Jetty and over all Customs launches on the river Unconfirmed reports had it that Japanese themselves raised the flags at 7.30 this morning. Office-goers saw it whipping in the breeze at 8 a.m.
Celebrates Session?
Questioned, Japanese sources declared that the "Reformed Government" flag was raised only for today to celebrate a session of the "Nanking Reformed Government" and the "Peking Provisional Government" at Nanking today, and would not be seen tomorrow. This could not be confirmed however.
Mr. L. H. Lawford, commissioner of Customs, and other foreign Customs officials were noncommittal about the significance of the change, when questioned by the Evening Post this morning. Mr. Y. Akatani, new administrative commissioner, however, indicated that the change had been made following a conference and at the request of the "Reformed Government."
Nothing To Say
"Owing to the circumstances here," one Chinese Customs employee said today, "we have nothing to say about the flag question." He refused to comment on a question as to whether there will be renewed agitation against the five-bar flag similar to that during the appointment of Li Chien-nan as "superintendent of the Shanghai Customs" by the "Reformed Government."
As result of the agitation against Mr. Li several Customs employees were transferred from Shanghai to other ports not under Japanese occupation. A Customs revenue guard, allegedly for his leadership during the demonstrations, was arrested by the Japanese and subsequently released after a prolonged detention.
History Recalled
Appearance of the five-bar flag this morning recalled the internal political and military strife during the first two decades of the Chinese Republic.
China had no national flags until late in the Manchu regime when the yellow flag with the traditional dragon was adopted as the national emblem of the Chinese Empire. It was said that Sir Robert Hart, organizer of the Chinese Customs, was responsible for prevailing upon the emperor to adopt a national flag.
When Dr. Sun Yat-sen launched his revolutionary movement, he designed in the late '90's the "blue-sky-white-sun" flag for the Kuomintang and the "blue-sky-white-sun-red-ground" flag to represent the Chinese Republic.
Confusion Resulted
There was a lot of confusion, however, when the revolutionary armies staged uprisings in various provinces. Some of the armies and revolutionary local governments adopted a red flag with a yellow star as the emblem.
When President Yuan Shih-kai was installed as the chief executive of the infant republic, he officially adopted the five-bar flag as the national emblem. The five colors, red, yellow, green, white and black, are meant to represent the unity of the five races of Han, Manchu, Mongol, Mohammedan and Tibetan.
Kuomintang circles, however, objected to the design, pointing out that the flag implies a racial barrier which should be removed in China. They advocated the tricolor flag representing "blue-sky-white-sun-red-ground." They adopted it as the national flag when they organized their own government in South China with Canton as the capital.
Officially Adopted
Upon the inauguration of the national government in Nanking in 1927, the tricolor was officially proclaimed the national flag and the five-bar flag abolished. Since then, the flag has been recognized throughout the world as the Chinese national emblem.
The five-bar flag, however, made its first appearance in a revised form in 1933 when Japan established "Manchukuo" in the occupied Manchurian provinces. The "Manchukuan" flag has the five colors with four bars and a prominent portion is in yellow—the color that represents Manchurians in the original five-bar flag.
Japanese-sponsored regimes in the occupied zone discarded the officially recognized national flag because of the implication that China is ruled by the Kuomintang, in that the party emblem of "green-sky-white-sun" is prominent on the background of "red ground," by pro-Japanese elements is a "bad omen" that China would be Bolshevized.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》。
1938年11月4日
海关升起
维新派旗帜
多年首次
在外滩见到
五色标志

今晨，作为中国帝国和早期共和国旧有的五色旗——如今是日本扶持的“维新政府”的标志——多年来首次在外滩上海海关大楼上方的桅杆上飘扬。

它取代了中国国民政府熟悉的三色旗，后者一直悬挂在那里，直到中国军队撤离上海。

这面红-黄-绿-白-黑五色的旗帜悬挂在海关大楼、码头上的海关查验所以及河上所有海关汽艇上。有未经证实的消息称，日本人自己在今早7点30分升起了这些旗帜。上班族在上午8点看到它在风中飘扬。

庆祝会议？
面对询问，日本方面声称，“维新政府”旗帜仅在今日悬挂，以庆祝今日在南京举行的“南京维新政府”和“北京临时政府”会议，明天将不再见到。但这无法得到证实。

今早《晚邮报》记者询问时，海关税务司 L. H. Lawford 先生和其他外籍海关官员对换旗的意义不予置评。然而，新任行政委员 Y. Akatani（音译）表示，换旗是在一次会议之后，应“维新政府”的要求进行的。

无可奉告
“鉴于这里的情况，”一位中国海关雇员今天说，“我们对旗帜问题无可奉告。”他拒绝评论是否会出现类似“维新政府”任命李建南为“上海海关总监”期间那样的针对五色旗的新抗议活动。

由于针对李先生的抗议，几名海关雇员被从上海调往其他未被日本占领的港口。一名海关缉私员据称因在示威期间的领导作用而被日本人逮捕，并在长期拘留后获释。

回顾历史
今晨五色旗的出现让人回想起中华民国前二十年的内部政治和军事纷争。

中国在满清政权晚期之前没有国旗，当时采用带有传统龙纹的黄旗作为中华帝国的国家象征。据说，中国海关的组织者赫德爵士（Sir Robert Hart）负责说服皇帝采用国旗。

当孙中山博士发起革命运动时，他在90年代后期为国民党设计了“青天白日”旗，并为中华共和国设计了“青天白日满地红”旗。

导致混乱
然而，当革命军在各省发动起义时，造成了很多混乱。一些军队和革命地方政府采用带有黄色星星的红旗作为标志。

当袁世凯总统就任新生共和国的元首时，他正式采用五色旗作为国家象征。五种颜色，红、黄、绿、白和黑，意在代表汉、满、蒙、回、藏五族共和。

然而，国民党圈子反对这一设计，指出该旗帜暗示了一种应在中国消除的种族壁垒。他们主张代表“青天白日满地红”的三色旗。当他们在华南以广州为首都组织自己的政府时，他们采用了它作为国旗。

正式采用
1927年南京国民政府成立后，三色旗被正式宣布为国旗，五色旗被废除。从此，该旗帜在世界范围内被公认为中国的国家象征。

然而，五色旗以修订形式首次出现于1933年，当时日本在被占领的满洲省份建立了“满洲国”。“满洲国”旗帜有五种颜色和四道条纹，其中显著部分是黄色——这在原始五色旗中代表满族人。

占领区的日本扶持政权丢弃了官方认可的国家旗帜，因为该旗帜暗示中国由国民党统治，即“青天白日”党徽在“满地红”背景上十分醒目，亲日分子认为这是中国将被布尔什维克化的“凶兆”。

November 3, 1938.

MAINTCHI

WHY DOES NOT THE CUSTOM HOUSE HOIST A FLAG?
By "Chokoitsujin" (pen name)

Every Custom House in every country
hoists a flag, but the Custom House in Shanghai does not
hoist any flag. It means that the Custom House does
not belong to anybody; it may give rise to a belief that
it belongs to bandits. Prior to the outbreak of the
Sino-Japanese hostilities, the Custom House belonged to
the National Government and hoisted the flag of the
National Government. After the occupation of Shanghai
by the Japanese army, the "Reformed Government" decided
to take over the Custom House. As a result of an
agreement reached between Mr. Li Chien Nan and Mr. Lawford,
the Custom House was transferred to the "Reformed Government".
According to the agreement made public,
one of the conditions stipulates that the five barred flag
of the "Reformed Government" shall be hoisted over the
Customs. It is only natural that the Customs should use
this flag, but the Customs never hoisted it. Already
half a year has elapsed since the "Reformed Government" took
over the Customs, yet no flag is being used by the Customs.
It is difficult for us to understand the attitude of the
"Reformed Government" in not taking proper steps in this
matter.

There is no necessity to fear the
Foreign Settlements because the transfer of the Customs to
the "Reformed Government" has been completely carried out
with recognition of the Government. We have captured
Canton and Hankow yet we still have the disheartening sight
of a flagless Customs at the mouth of the Yangtze River.

（左侧手写批注：）

pages.zh:
1938年11月3日。

MAINTCHI

海关为何不悬挂旗帜？
作者：“Chokoitsujin”（笔名）

各国的海关均悬挂旗帜，唯独上海海关不悬挂任何旗帜。这意味着海关不属于任何人；这可能会让人产生一种信念，认为它属于匪徒。在中日敌对行动爆发之前，海关属于国民政府，并悬挂国民政府的旗帜。日军占领上海后，“维新政府”决定接管海关。经李健南先生与乐斐蕃（Lawford）先生达成协议，海关被移交给“维新政府”。根据公布的协议，其中一项条件规定，海关应悬挂“维新政府”的五色旗。海关使用这面旗帜本是理所当然之事，但海关从未悬挂过。自“维新政府”接管海关以来，半年时间已过，然而海关仍未使用任何旗帜。我们难以理解“维新政府”在此事上未采取适当措施的态度。

没有必要害怕外国租界，因为海关向“维新政府”的移交已在该政府获得承认的情况下完全执行。我们已攻占广州和汉口，但在长江口看到海关无旗可挂的景象，仍令人沮丧。

（左侧手写批注：）
12月3日
30/2
31"

pages.en:
( 2 )

When we consider the victory won by our army at a great
sacrifice it is a matter for great indignation to witness
such a situation.

I repeat: the five barred flag must
be hoisted over the Customs in Shanghai. This Customs
belongs to the "Reformed Government" which is founded by
pro-Japanese Chinese in Central China. The Customs
should declare to the world that it is the Customs of the
"Reformed Government" by hoisting this flag. Should the
Customs ignore our advice and fail to hoist the flag, the
officers of the Customs who are opposing it should be
removed. As everybody knows, most of the important
positions in the Customs are held by British subjects,
but such a condition is not stipulated in any treaty, it
is due to the fact that the revenue of the Customs had
been mortgaged against foreign loans.

The "Reformed Government" should press
the Customs authorities to hoist the five barred flag.
If the authorities maintain that the use of this flag by
the Customs will ~~bring~~ endanger their lives and obstruct
the discharge of their duties, because of the presence of
a menacing atmosphere in the Settlement, the "Reformed
Government" should dispatch soldiers to protect them. If
the Settlement authorities oppose this measure they should
be held responsible for the protection of the Customs
officers. If The Municipal authorities say that they are
not in a position to protect the Customs officers, they
should then be requested to hand over to the Japanese the
authority to maintain peace and order in the Settlement.
If the Customs authorities refuse to hoist the flag, then
the "Reformed Government" should immediately remove these
authorities and appoint suitable persons to replace them.
pages.zh:
( 2 )

考虑到我军以巨大牺牲换来的胜利，目睹此种情形实令人愤慨不已。

我重申：必须在上海海关悬挂五色旗。该海关属于由华中亲华人士建立的“维新政府”。海关应通过悬挂此旗向世界宣告，它是“维新政府”的海关。如果海关无视我们的建议而不悬挂旗帜，则应撤换反对悬挂旗帜的海关官员。众所周知，海关的重要职位大多由英国臣民担任，但任何条约中并未规定此种状况，这是由于海关税收已被抵押用于偿还外债所致。

“维新政府”应向海关当局施压，要求其悬挂五色旗。如果当局声称，由于租界内存在威胁气氛，海关使用此旗将~~带来~~危及其生命并阻碍其履行职责，那么“维新政府”应派遣士兵保护他们。如果租界当局反对这一措施，则应由他们负责保护海关官员。如果工部局当局表示无力保护海关官员，则应要求他们将维持租界治安的权力移交给日本人。如果海关当局拒绝悬挂旗帜，那么“维新政府”应立即撤换这些官员，并任命合适的人选接替。

pages.en:
( 3 )

Great improvements have taken place
in conditions in Central and South China since May this
year. The situation has already reached such a state
that something must be done about the existence of the
Foreign Settlements for they are being used as a base
for anti-Japanese activities.

It is to be hoped that at an important
time like the present, the Shanghai Customs will hoist
the five barred flag and support the activities of the

pages.zh:
( 3 )

自今年五月以来，华中和华南地区的状况已有极大改善。局势已发展到必须对外国租界的存续采取行动的地步，因为它们正被用作反日活动的基地。

希望在当前这一重要时刻，上海海关能悬挂五色旗，并支持“维新政府”在外国租界内的活动。

pages.en:
November 7, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta Kei Tao and other local newspapers:

THE HOISTING OF A FIVE-BARRED FLAG ON THE CUSTOMS
BUILDING

The Chinese employees of the Customs have been very indignant over the forcible changing of the flag above the Customs building. The matter is at present receiving much attention from both foreigners and Chinese. According to the usual practice, the national flag is hoisted on the Customs building on Sundays, but this was not done yesterday. Five-barred flags were hoisted both on the building and the Customs jetty. Moreover, these flags have been displayed on all the Customs boats since Friday last. It is unbelievable that the five-barred flag was hoisted on the Customs building on Friday surreptitiously. It is said that hereafter these flags will be hoisted every Sunday and the anniversaries observed by the "Reformed Government". Mr. Lawford, Commissioner of Customs, has so far refused to make any statement regarding this affair.

According to information secured from parties concerned yesterday by the Sin Shun News Agency (新申社), the Chinese employees of the Customs do not contemplate taking any action in connection with this matter prior to receipt of telegraphic instructions from the National Government.

According to a certain high Chinese official of the Customs, the flag was hoisted by the Japanese employees of the Customs in conspiracy with the puppet authorities; the Customs authorities were entirely ignorant of the affair before the flag was hoisted. That this flag could have again appeared on the Customs building yesterday after the negotiations is apparently due to the action of the Japanese employees of the Customs. The official further said that it was difficult to foretell at present whether or not the Customs would be forced to change its flag.

It is said that Mr. Lawford, Commissioner of Customs, after his receipt of the information that the five-barred flag had again appeared on the Customs building, at once communicated with the Japanese Consul-General by telephone, but the latter refused to undertake the negotiations, stating that the matter was one relating to the "Reformed Government" which had practically nothing to do with the Japanese authorities. According to the foreign observers, the Chinese employees of the Customs will probably unite to deal with this matter in case of necessity.

The flag which was hoisted over the Customs building yesterday was removed at about 5 p.m. A meeting was held at a certain place yesterday by a number of Chinese employees of the Customs, and it is said that they are about to issue a manifesto in connection with this affair.
pages.zh:
1938年11月7日。晨间翻译。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

海关大楼悬挂五色旗

海关中国职员对海关大楼上方旗帜被强行更换一事感到非常愤怒。此事目前受到外国人和中国人的广泛关注。按照惯例，海关大楼于星期日悬挂国旗，但昨日并未这样做。大楼及海关码头均悬挂了五色旗。此外，自上周五以来，所有海关船只也都展示了这些旗帜。令人难以置信的是，五色旗于周五被偷偷悬挂在海关大楼上。据说，此后每逢星期日及“维新政府”纪念日均将悬挂这些旗帜。海关税务司乐斐蕃（Lawford）先生至今拒绝对此事发表任何声明。

据新申社（Sin Shun News Agency）昨日从有关方面获悉的消息，海关中国职员在收到国民政府的电报指示之前，不打算就此事项采取任何行动。

据海关某位高级中国官员称，旗帜是由海关日本职员与傀儡当局合谋悬挂的；在旗帜悬挂之前，海关当局对此事完全不知情。经过谈判后，昨日该旗帜再次出现在海关大楼上，显然归因于海关日本职员的行动。该官员进一步表示，目前难以预测海关是否会被迫更换旗帜。

据说，海关税务司乐斐蕃先生在得知五色旗再次出现在海关大楼上的消息后，立即通过电话与日本总领事联系，但后者拒绝进行交涉，称此事涉及“维新政府”，与日本当局几乎无关。据外国观察家称，如有必要，海关中国职员可能会联合起来处理此事。

昨日悬挂在海关大楼上的旗帜于下午5点左右被移除。昨日，多名海关中国职员在某地举行会议，据悉他们即将就此事发表宣言。

pages.en:
Chinese-American Daily News (Comment):

Three days have elapsed since the change of
the flag by the Customs. Nothing has been made known to
the public of the motive of this change nor has any action
been taken.
The Customs authorities are in the employ of
the Chinese National Government. They should be held
responsible for the appearance within their administration
of a flag which represents an organization betraying the
Government. It is said that this change of flag on the
part of the Customs was made under compulsion, and if this
is so, their act is somewhat pardonable, otherwise they
cannot evade their responsibilities in connection with this
affair.
pages.zh:
《中美日报》（评论）：

海关换旗已过去三天。公众尚未知晓此次换旗的动机，也未采取任何行动。
海关当局受雇于中国国民政府。对于在其管理范围内出现代表背叛政府组织的旗帜，他们应承担责任。据说海关此次换旗是被迫进行的，如果是这样，其行为尚可宽恕，否则他们无法逃避与此事相关的责任。

pages.en:
Ta Mei Pao :•

FIVE-BARRED FLAGS OVER CUSTOMS AND HARBOUR OFFICE

With reference to the five-barred flags flying
over the Customs and the Harbour Office yesterday, enquiries
made by a reporter of the Ta Tung News Agency ( 大通通訊社 )
show that the flags were hoisted on the roofs of the Customs
and the Harbour Office by three Japanese uniformed men and
several Japanese detectives of the River Police.
Whilst the flag was being hoisted over the
Customs, foreign and Japanese uniformed men of the River
Police were posted on guard at the main entrance on The Bund
as well as the side entrances on Hankow Road and Szechuen
Road. They did not withdraw until noon. Up to the evening,
however, two Japanese river policemen were posted for duty
on the roof where the flag was hoisted.
pages.zh:
《大美报》：

海关与港务局上空飘扬五色旗

关于昨日海关与港务局上空飘扬的五色旗，大通通讯社（Ta Tung News Agency）记者进行的调查显示，这些旗帜是由三名身穿制服的日本人和几名水上警察局的日本侦探悬挂在海关和港务局屋顶上的。
当旗帜在海关上空悬挂时，水上警察局的外国和日本制服人员在外滩正门以及汉口路和四川路的侧门站岗警戒。他们直到中午才撤离。然而，直到晚上，仍有两名日本水上警察在悬挂旗帜的屋顶上执勤。

pages.en:
November 5, 1938. Morning Translation.

Morning Leader (Editorial):

The Changing of Flags by the Shanghai Customs

Yesterday a five-barred flag of the puppet organization was hoisted over the Customs House. Our paper is British, and when we see the bogus flag over the Customs House, we have a feeling that every Chinese and upright foreigner is looking at the flag with a hatred against Great Britain. Of course it is Japan and not Great Britain who has seized the Customs, but how could Japan have openly seized an organ that has more or less an international character if the Chamberlain Government had not adopted a policy of compromise and submission?
The Chinese are angry while the Japanese rejoice to see this five-barred flag. As for the British, they should be ashamed.
Upon the establishment of the "Reformed Government of the Chinese Republic", a Customs Agreement was concluded between Britain and Japan. Subsequently the Customs receipts, minus payments for foreign loans, were deposited in the Japanese Yokohama Specie Bank. The deposits were made in the name of the Commissioner of the Shanghai Maritime Customs instead of the Inspector-General of Customs as was usually done. With the hoisting of the bogus flag, the Shanghai Customs has fallen into Japanese hands both nominally and practically.
The changing of flag by the Customs at this moment is without doubt attributable to the fall of Hankow and Canton and the exposure of the weakness of the Chamberlain Government. Since the adoption of a policy of compromise and submission by Chamberlain, and especially after the Munich Conference, the aggressors have clearly seen that Britain will make concessions at every threat, the extent of the concessions increasing in proportion to the threat, and is ready to sacrifice not only others' interests, but even her own. Although Japan realizes that the capture of Hankow and Canton only means increased difficulties, she knows that the victory, even if it is only vain glory, will be useful to scare Britain. Since the occupation of Wuhan, Japan has done her best both in words and acts to wreck British interests in China. On the other hand, Chamberlain has said that "anyone who wishes to reconstruct China will need the assistance of Britain" while the British Under-Secretary for Foreign Affairs has said that it may be hoped that Japan will soon satisfy all parties in England, showing that certain short-sighted British officials have virtually recognized Japanese control of China.
As General Chiang Kai-shek has said, China will continue to fight and no changes in the international situation will stop China from driving back her invaders. Anyone who hopes to get some leavings from the aggressors at the expense of China's friendship will only bring about the destruction of his own interests.
pages.zh:
1938年11月5日。晨间翻译。

《字林西报》（社论）：

上海海关换旗

昨日，伪组织的五色旗被悬挂在海关大楼上。本报属英资背景，当我们看到海关大楼上挂着这面假旗时，感觉每一个中国人和正直的外国人都在怀着对英国的仇恨注视着这面旗帜。当然，夺取海关的是日本而非英国，但如果张伯伦政府没有采取妥协与屈服的政策，日本怎敢公然夺取一个具有某种国际性质的机构？
中国人对此感到愤怒，而日本人则因看到这面五色旗而欣喜。至于英国人，他们应当感到羞耻。
在“中华民国维新政府”成立之际，英国与日本达成了一项海关协定。随后，海关收入在扣除外债偿付款项后，存入日本横滨正金银行。存款是以上海海关税务司的名义进行的，而不是像通常那样以海关总税务司的名义进行。随着假旗的悬挂，上海海关在名义上和实际上都落入了日本人手中。
海关此时换旗，无疑归因于汉口和广州的陷落，以及张伯伦政府软弱性的暴露。自从张伯伦采取妥协与屈服政策，特别是慕尼黑会议之后，侵略者清楚地看到，英国会在每一次威胁下做出让步，让步的程度与威胁的大小成正比，并且准备不仅牺牲他人的利益，甚至牺牲自己的利益。虽然日本意识到占领汉口和广州只意味着困难的增加，但她知道，即使是虚名般的胜利，也有助于恐吓英国。自占领武汉以来，日本在言论和行动上都竭力破坏英国在华利益。另一方面，张伯伦称“任何希望重建中国的人都需要英国的协助”，而英国外交部次长则表示，希望日本能很快让英国各方满意，这表明某些短视的英国官员实际上已经承认了日本对中国的控制。
正如蒋介石将军所言，中国将继续战斗，国际局势的任何变化都不会阻止中国驱逐侵略者。任何希望以牺牲中国友谊为代价从侵略者那里得到残羹剩饭的人，只会导致自身利益的毁灭。

pages.en:
November 5, 1938. Morning Translation.

News Digest publishes the following leading article :-

Under Japanese pressure, the Shanghai Maritime Customs yesterday morning hoisted a five-barred flag. At a casual glance, the change of flag seems to be strange, but in reality is a natural sequence of Mr. Chamberlain's diplomatic policy.

Sometime ago Britain and Japan concluded a Customs agreement which permitted the appointment of a Superintendent of Customs by the 'Reformed Government" and the deposit of revenues with the Yokohama Specie Bank. This agreement is a violation of the principle of the League of Nations refusing recognition of all unlawful annexations and is a compromise to the fait accompli caused by Japan through armed force. Fortunately due to strong opposition of the Chinese staff of the Customs and the indignation of the local foreign and Chinese community, the puppet Customs Superintendent dared not exercise his functions openly and the bogus flag was prevented from flying over the Customs. After permitting the Japanese to complete their preliminary control of the Customs, the adherents of Mr. Chamberlain's policy even afforded the Japanese the facilities of examination, consented to an increase of Japanese employees on the Customs and allowed the Customs to enforce the tariff which is drawn up by the "Reformed Government" and which is favourable to Japanese imports. Therefore, the Customs has become a protective organ of Japanese trade.

In a public statement, Mr. Shiratori, Japanese Ambassador to Italy, declared that Japan would make Britain's interests in the Far East shrink, which assertion Mr. Chamberlain met with a smiling face and predicted in the British Parliament that Japan would have sole control of China's market. Mr. Chamberlain's speech abets the ambitions of the Japanese warlords and will lead them into a belief that no matter how arrogant their activities are, they will certainly get compromise from Britain. The change of flag is simply one of the instances in point.

Possibly the hoisting of the five-barred flag by the Customs is regarded as a trivial matter by the gentlemen of Mr. Chamberlain's ilk. However, the thing is not as trifling as it appears. Firstly, it violates the administration of Chinese Customs; secondly, it signifies Japan's further ignorance of the prestige in China of Britain and other foreign Powers, and thirdly it may cause a great disturbance and impair the revenue required by Britain.

In view of the foregoing, we hope that Britain and the other Powers, who have relations with the Chinese Customs, will, for the sake of their own interests, exert joint pressure on the Japanese and demand the immediate removal of the five-barred flag. Britain and other Powers should understand that Japan's resources are about to be exhausted by China's 16 months war of resistance and that she is showing signs of exhaustion in dealing with China alone. Where has she the strength to cope with you? She is bound to yield if you will exercise the pressure. On the contrary, the more you give up your ground, the more Japan will demand, and by that time all your interests in China will have been seized by her. Britain, France and America, rise up jointly to protest against the flying of the bogus flag by the Customs and the whole Chinese community in Shanghai as well as the entire body of the Customs employees will naturally support you.
pages.zh:
1938年11月5日。晨间译稿。

《新闻报》发表如下社论：

在日本的压力下，上海海关于昨日上午悬挂了五色旗。乍看之下，换旗之举似乎有些奇怪，但实际上这是张伯伦先生外交政策的自然结果。

不久前，英国与日本达成了一项海关协定，允许“维新政府”任命海关税务司，并将税款存入横滨正金银行。这项协定违反了国际联盟拒绝承认一切非法吞并的原则，是对日本通过武力造成的既成事实的妥协。幸运的是，由于海关华籍职员的强烈反对以及当地外侨和华人社区的愤慨，傀儡海关税务司不敢公开行使职权，伪旗也未能悬挂在海关大楼之上。在允许日本人完成对海关的初步控制后，张伯伦政策的追随者甚至为日本人提供便利，同意增加海关中的日籍雇员，并允许海关执行由“维新政府”制定的、有利于日本进口的关税税率。因此，海关已沦为日本贸易的保护机构。

日本驻意大利大使白鸟敏夫在一份公开声明中宣称，日本将使英国在远东的利益萎缩，张伯伦先生对此报以微笑，并在英国议会中预言日本将独占中国市场。张伯伦的讲话助长了日本军阀的野心，会使他们相信，无论其行动多么傲慢，必定能得到英国的妥协。换旗 simply 是其中一个例证。

也许，对于张伯伦之流的人物来说，海关悬挂五色旗被视为一件小事。然而，此事并不像表面看起来那样微不足道。首先，它违反了中国海关的行政管理；其次，它表明日本进一步无视英国及其他外国列强在中国的威望；第三，它可能引起巨大动荡，并损害英国所需的财政收入。

鉴于上述情况，我们希望与中国海关有关系的英国及其他列强，为了自身利益，共同向日本施加压力，要求立即撤下五色旗。英国及其他列强应当明白，日本的资源因中国16个月的抗战而即将耗尽，她在单独对付中国时已显出疲态。她哪里还有力量来应付你们？如果你们施加压力，她必然屈服。相反，你们越是放弃立场，日本的要求就越多，到那时，你们在中国的所有利益都将被她攫取。英、法、美三国联合起来抗议海关悬挂伪旗，上海全体华人社区以及全体海关职员自然会支持你们。

pages.en:
November 5, 1938. Morning Translation

Hwa Mei Chen Pao publishes the following leading article :-

It was due to the belief on the part of the
Chamberlain Government that Hitler's annexation of the
Sudeten area in Czechoslovakia was his final territorial
demand in Europe that a "disgraceful" peace was
reached at the Munich conference. It is also
due to the belief on the part of the Chamberlain Government
that the assurances given by both Mussolini and Hitler that
they have no territorial designs in Spain that the
enforcement of the British-Italian pact could likewise be
realized. It is known to all what real weight the promises
of the Fascists carry.

As a matter
of fact no explanation for such promises is necessary. It
is absurd to assume that Premier Chamberlain could have fallen
short of such an understanding. But, after all, how is it
that he has acted so contrary to the wishes of the general
public? To tell the truth, there is nothing unusual in
this; it is due to his principles and to his own interests.
In other words, so long as the question of interests is
concerned, Chamberlain is willing to sacrifice not only
righteousness and justice, but also weak and friendly nations
and if it is necessary he is even willing to sacrifice the
interests of his country.

If Chamberlain believes that Germany and Italy have
no territorial designs in Europe, then by the same token he
must likewise believe the assurances of the Japanese
Fascist militarists that they have no territorial ambitions
in China. This, indeed, is the view of Premier Chamberlain,
as witness his statement in the House of Commons, when he
pointed out that even if Japan could secure complete control
of China, she could not carry out her plans for development
without British co-operation. He also emphasized that
whoever desired to undertake the reconstruction of China
could not do so without help from Great Britain. It is for
this reason that the Chamberlain Government has been anxious
to please Japan despite the fact that the latter has been
doing her utmost to oust British interests from China. That
this is true can be proved by the statement, made by the
British Vice Foreign Secretary, that the negotiations at
present in progress between Britain and Japan would result
in a satisfactory outcome for the British.

Premier Chamberlain's only desire is to direct
the "arrow" of the Fascists towards Soviet Russia. It is
due to this desire that he has "instigated" his "imaginary
foes" to direct their "anger" against the U.S.S.R. Not
only is he unwilling to extinguish the "flames" of the
aggressors, but he is, on the contrary, supplying them with
materials. That the Chamberlain Government can have adopted
such an "inflammatory policy" in Europe convinces us that
it can likewise adopt a similar policy in the Far East.
That is to say, in order to please the Japanese militarists
and to maintain his interests in China, he is willing to
act as rearguard for the Japanese Fascist militarists and
to recognize Japanese aggression in China as a campaign
against the Comintern.
pages.zh:
1938年11月5日。晨间译稿

《华美晨报》发表如下社论：

正是由于张伯伦政府相信希特勒吞并捷克斯洛伐克的苏台德地区是他在欧洲的最后领土要求，慕尼黑会议才达成了“可耻的”和平。同样，由于张伯伦政府相信墨索里尼和希特勒所作的他们在西班牙没有领土野心的保证，英意协定的执行才得以实现。众所周知，法西斯分子的承诺究竟有多大的分量。

事实上，对此类承诺无需多加解释。假设张伯伦首相缺乏这种理解是荒谬的。但毕竟，他为何如此违背公众的意愿？说实话，这并无不寻常之处；这是出于他的原则和他自身的利益。换句话说，只要涉及利益问题，张伯伦不仅愿意牺牲道义和正义，还愿意牺牲弱小的友好国家，如果有必要，他甚至愿意牺牲本国的利益。

如果张伯伦相信德国和意大利在欧洲没有领土野心，那么同理，他也必须相信日本法西斯军国主义者所作的他们在中国没有领土野心的保证。这确实是张伯伦首相的观点，正如他在下议院的声明所见证的那样，他指出，即使日本能够完全控制中国，如果没有英国的合作，她也无法实施其发展计划。他还强调，任何想要从事中国重建工作的人，都离不开大不列颠的帮助。正因为这个原因，尽管日本正竭尽全力将英国利益逐出中国，张伯伦政府仍急于讨好日本。英国外交部次官发表的声明证明了这一点，该声明称，目前英日之间的谈判将为英国带来令人满意的结果。

张伯伦首相唯一的愿望是将法西斯主义的“箭矢”引向苏联俄罗斯。正是出于这种愿望，他“煽动”他的“假想敌”将他们的“愤怒”指向苏联。他不仅不愿意熄灭侵略者的“火焰”，反而向他们提供物资。张伯伦政府能在欧洲采取这种“煽动性政策”，这使我们确信，它在远东也能采取类似的政策。也就是说，为了讨好日本军国主义者并维持其在中国的利益，他愿意充当日本法西斯军国主义者的后卫，并将日本对中国的侵略认可为反共产国际的运动。

pages.en:
We have to remind the British people that the
"inflammatory policy" of Premier Chamberlain will be
suicidal to Great Britain. Even if the British people
give no regard to public righteousness and justice,
they should, however, do something in the interests of
the future prospects of their country. The opponents
of the Fascist nations to-day are Britain and France but
not the U.S.S.R. This is a fact clear to all. As regards
China, she will remain Chinese. Britain cannot benefit
if she intends to compel China to submit to Japan.
Whereas the British Government is at present
doing everything possible to placate Japan, the U.S.
Government has lodged strong and stern protests with
Tokyo. In justice, we cannot but say that there is a
great deal of difference between the wisdom of the
statesmen of the two big Anglo-Saxon nations.
pages.zh: 我们必须提醒英国人民，张伯伦首相的“煽动性政策”将对大不列颠造成自杀性的后果。即使英国人民不顾公共道义和正义，他们也应当为了国家未来的前景做些事情。今天法西斯国家的对手是英国和法国，而不是苏联。这是一个所有人都清楚的事实。至于中国，她将始终是中国。如果英国企图迫使中国屈服于日本，英国将无法从中受益。然而，当英国政府目前正尽一切可能安抚日本时，美国政府已向东京提出了强烈而严厉的抗议。公正地说，我们不得不说，这两个盎格鲁-撒克逊大国的政治家们在智慧上存在很大差异。

CHINA PRESS.

NOV 5 1938

No Change
Indicated By
5-Bar Flag
On Customs

High Official Declares
Customs Integrity Is
Undisturbed

BRITISH PAYING
CLOSE ATTENTION

Local Business Circles
Unperturbed Over
New Emblem

The appearance of the five-bar flag over the Custom House, the Harbor Office and on river vessels of the Chinese Maritime Customs yesterday has little significance and the integrity of the Customs is undisturbed, THE CHINA PRESS was informed by a high Customs official yesterday.

Besides this vague, ambiguous statement, however, THE CHINA PRESS could learn no reason why a year after the Japanese first occupied Shanghai, the five-bar flag of the "Reformed Government" suddenly made its reappearance over the Customs House yesterday.

Shanghailanders were somewhat surprised yesterday morning when they spotted a brand new five-barred banner of gigantic dimensions fluttering from the high mast over Big Ching, the Customs clock. The Harbor Office across the road also displayed the multicolored banner. Later, it was discovered that the Customs fire floats and launches also flew this flag.

Refuses To Comment

Mr. L. H. Lawford, Commissioner of Customs, when questioned by THE CHINA PRESS yesterday, regretted that he was not in a position to communicate with the press. Mr. Y. Akatani, new administrative commissioner, also revealed little, replying that he was not authorised to make any statement.

No satisfaction could be obtained from the British Consular authorities either, they merely stating that the British Consulate-General here was paying close attention to the matter, which, they added, was "not worth getting excited about."

A statement, attributed to Japanese sources yesterday, that the flags were raised only for one day to celebrate a session of the "Reformed" and "Provisional" puppet regimes at Nanking yesterday was treated lightly by well-informed circles who, although they did not believe this explanation to be true refused to replace it with a better one.

Makes Blunt Statement

Perhaps the most tangible comment on the hoisting of the five-bar flags came from the blunt foreign Customs official who told a representative of THE CHINA PRESS that "Whether we like it or not, we can't run the Customs without the Japanese."

Foreign business circles here, however, also failed to attach particular significance to the raising of the flags. They pointed out that such flags were already flying over all Customs buildings in Japanese-occupied territory.

The five-barred flag, which has been resurrected by the puppet regimes, was the Chinese national flag until, in 1927, it was abolished and gave place to the present white-sun-blue-sky flag.

The multicolored banner made its first appearance after the 1911 revolution, when President Yuan Shih-kai, chief executive of the new republic, adopted it as the national emblem. The five colors, red, yellow, green, white and black represent the unity of the five Chinese races, Han, Manchu, Mongol, Mohammedan and Tibetan.

The Kuomintang in 1927 abolished this flag because it implied a racial barrier between the Chinese people. It was then that the white sun, set in a blue sky and a red background was adopted as the National Flag.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。

1938年11月5日

海关悬挂
五色旗并未
显示变化

高官宣称
海关完整性
未受干扰

英国方面
密切关注

本地商界
对新标志
不为所动

据一位海关高级官员昨日向《字林西报》透露，昨日中国海关在海关大楼、港务处及河面船只上悬挂五色旗一事意义不大，海关的完整性未受干扰。

然而，除了这一模糊、模棱两可的声明外，《字林西报》未能获悉为何在日本首次占领上海一年后，“维新政府”的五色旗昨日突然重新出现在海关大楼之上。

昨日早晨，当上海外侨发现一面巨大的全新五色旗帜在海关钟楼（Big Ching）的高桅杆上飘扬时，感到有些惊讶。马路对面的港务处也展示了这面多色旗帜。后来发现，海关的消防船和汽艇也悬挂了这面旗帜。

拒绝评论

海关税务司劳福德（L. H. Lawford）先生昨日在接受《字林西报》询问时，遗憾地表示他无法与媒体沟通。新任行政税务司赤谷（Y. Akatani，音译）先生也透露甚少，回复称他无权发表任何声明。

英国领事当局也未提供任何令人满意的答复，他们仅表示英国驻沪总领事馆正在密切关注此事，并补充说此事“不值得大惊小怪”。

昨日有归因于日本方面的说法称，悬挂旗帜仅是为了庆祝昨日在南京举行的“维新”和“临时”傀儡政权的一次会议，这一说法被消息灵通人士轻描淡写地对待，他们虽然不相信这一解释是真实的，但也拒绝用更好的解释来替代它。

直言不讳的声明

或许关于悬挂五色旗最切实的评论来自一位直言不讳的外籍海关官员，他告诉《字林西报》的代表：“无论我们喜欢与否，没有日本人我们就无法运营海关。”

然而，本地的外籍商界也未赋予升旗特别的 significance。他们指出，在日本占领区的所有海关建筑上已经悬挂着此类旗帜。

五色旗是被傀儡政权重新启用的，它曾是中国的国旗，直到1927年被废除，让位于现在的青天白日满地红旗。

这面多色旗帜在1911年革命后首次出现，当时新共和国的首任总统袁世凯将其采用为国家标志。五种颜色——红、黄、绿、白、黑——代表汉、满、蒙、回、藏五族共和。

国民党在1927年废除了这面旗帜，因为它暗示了中国人民之间的种族隔阂。就在那时，蓝底、红地、白日图案被采纳为国旗。

FRENCH POLICE DAILY REPORT
November 5, 1938.

At 7.30 a.m. November 4, representatives of the
Japanese Naval Authorities, accompanied by Japanese
members of the River Police presented themselves at
the Custom House where they hoisted the five-barred
flag (emblem of the Reformed Government) over the
buildings and Customs' vessels. The Chinese employees
of the Customs were most indignant at this display.
Mr. KIUTSO CHI, Chinese Commissioner of Customs in
Shanghai being absent due to poor health, the Chinese
employees made no protest and carried out their normal
duties during the day. They intend, however, to
request Mr. LAWFORD, the Commissioner, to negotiate
with the Japanese to have the Reformed Government's
flags not hoisted. They are said to have considered
launching a strike in the event of satisfaction not
being obtained.

Date MAY 18, 1938.
Subject Extract from "Standard" May 16th issue regarding letter addressed to Chinese employees of the Customs by "Shanghai Progressive Reading Society."
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Reference the attached translation of an extract from the May 16th issue of the "Standard" entitled "Letter addressed to the Chinese employees of the Customs by the Shanghai Progressive Reading Society," there is no record of this society in any of the Shanghai Municipal Police registries nor is it known to the Special Branch.

On the afternoon of 13/5/38, Mr. P.L. Hien (**〔此处转录不清〕**), Chinese manager of the "Standard," was interviewed at Special Branch, Headquarters, when he produced the original letter which he stated had been delivered to his office by ordinary mail, the sender being unknown. Examination of the letter shows that there is no mention in it of the Shanghai Progressive Reading Society, but that name is written on a piece of paper pasted to the letter. When asked to explain this fact, Mr. Hien stated that the piece of the letter on which the name of the Society was written was accidentally cut off and mislaid. As the letter appears to have been mimeographed, it is possible that it was sent to the "Standard" by some person interested in fostering unrest among Customs employees and that the name "Shanghai Progressive Reading Society" was substituted by the editor of the "Standard."

Mr. Hien was warned against publishing such matter in the future. In reply he expressed regret and promised to be more careful.

Mr. H.M. Cumine, Secretary to the Wen Wei Co., proprietor of the "Standard," is at present indisposed and does not attend office.

D.C. (Special Branch)

主题 摘自5月16日《标准晚报》关于“上海进步读书会”致海关中国职员的信件的摘录。
由副督察长洛根（Logan）制作 转呈者 **〔此处转录不清〕**

关于附件中翻译的5月16日《标准晚报》题为“上海进步读书会致海关中国职员的信”的摘录，在上海公共租界工部局警务处的任何登记册中均无该团体的记录，特别股也不知晓该团体。

1938年5月13日下午，《标准晚报》华籍经理贤先生（P.L. Hien，**〔此处转录不清〕**）在总部特别股接受问询，他出示了原件信件，并称该信是通过普通邮件送达其办公室的，寄件人不明。经检查信件，信中并未提及“上海进步读书会”，但该名称写在粘贴于信上的一张纸条上。当被要求解释这一事实时，贤先生称写有该团体名称的那部分信件被意外剪掉并遗失。由于该信似乎是油印的，有可能是某位有意在海关职员中煽动不安的人寄给《标准晚报》的，而“上海进步读书会”这一名称是由《标准晚报》编辑添加的。

贤先生受到警告，不得在未来刊登此类内容。作为回应，他表示遗憾并承诺会更加谨慎。

《标准晚报》所有者文汇公司秘书库明（H.M. Cumine）先生目前身体不适，未去办公室上班。

May 16, 1938. Morning Translation.

Standard published on May 14 the following letter addressed
to the Chinese employees of the Customs by the Shanghai
Progressive Reading Society :-

Not satisfied with the invasion of our
country, the massacre of our fellow countrymen and
raping of our sisters, the ferocious and merciless
Japanese imperialists are now attempting to seize
control of our Customs revenue in the hope of accelerating
the downfall of our nation.
We were deeply touched by the manifesto
issued by you on May 8. Brave Customs employees, your
courageous fighting spirit will spread far and wide
and will bring us more international support and because
of your spirit, the Government will be more determined
to carry on the war of resistance, while the people
throughout the country will become more confident of
final victory. We extend you our deepest respect and
assure that we are prepared to render you every support.
We are willing to die with you for our nation's
independence and emancipation. Brave Customs employees,
carry on courageously; the whole nation is with you!
Let us shout:-
"Long live the movement promoted by the
Chinese employees of the Customs for the protection of
the Customs:
"Long live the Republic of China!"

DSS ~gan
E. 1/2

1938年5月16日。晨间翻译。

《标准晚报》于5月14日刊登了以下由上海进步读书会致海关中国职员的信件：-

凶残无情的日本帝国主义者不满足于侵略我国、屠杀我国同胞和强奸我国姐妹，现在正试图夺取我国海关收入的控制权，以期加速我国的灭亡。
我们对你们于5月8日发表的宣言深为感动。勇敢的海关职员们，你们英勇的战斗精神将广泛传播，并将为我们带来更多的国际支持；因为你们的精神，政府将更加坚定地继续进行抗战，而全国人民将对最终胜利更有信心。我们向你们致以最深的敬意，并保证准备给予你们一切支持。我们愿意为国家的独立和解放与你们同生共死。勇敢的海关职员们，继续勇敢战斗；全国人民与你们同在！
让我们高呼：-
“海关中国职员保护海关运动万岁：
“中华民国万岁！”

DSS ~gan
E. 1/2

Translation of handbill

manifesto issued by students in Shanghai in support of the
customs employees in opposing the taking over of the customs
by a bogus organization.

A glorious and sacred struggle against the taking over
of the customs by the bogus organization was begun by the
entire body of Chinese employees on May 8. This association
regards the struggle as one staged by our patriotic and freedom
loving people against Japanese imperialists who have occupied
a large portion of our territory and massacred a large number
of our brethren, and who have the intention of enslaving the
whole Chinese race. The struggle is also one of our loyal
and gallant people against traitors and national betrayers.
This association hereby declares that it is the duty of
every Chinese citizen in Shanghai to struggle against any
bogus organization formed by traitors. The Chinese members
of the staff of the customs are the vanguard of the three
million people in Shanghai. The struggle has been started
by these customs employees in response to the demand of the
three million people. Thousands of students in our colleges,
middle and primary schools are determined not to allow the
traitors and national betrayers to become active in Shanghai,
nor permit them to realize their aim of taking over
the customs by trickery. We have sworn to support the
Chinese customs employees who command our respect.

The customs revenue is the principal source of our
national income, and the Shanghai customs is the key to China's
import and export trade. Therefore, the revenue from the
Shanghai customs forms the principal part of our national income.
The invaders have instigated national traitors connected with
bogus organizations to attempt to take over the customs. If
we, the citizens of Shanghai, do not protect the customs
and allow the Japanese invaders to take it over, the result
will be that (1) the national government will suffer financially,
leading to a reduction in the strength of resistance; (2) the
Japanese invaders will revise the customs tariff in such a way
as to destroy China's import and export trade; (3) the Japanese
invaders will be able to replenish their war chest, which is in
process of depletion in consequence of the protracted war now
in progress. This association considers it the duty of every
Chinese citizen in Shanghai to prevent the Japanese invaders
from realizing their object. The announcement (see the
manifesto issued by the Chinese customs employees) that they
are determined not to cooperate with any bogus organization which
is harmful to the interests of the nation and the race and
are opposed to the depositing of customs revenue in the Yokohama
Specie Bank, represents what we are demanding.

To-day, May 10, when we saw the cruel Japanese arrest
Mr. Yang Wen Loong, a revenue guard by force, we immediately
knew how knavish and shameless the Japanese imperialists are.
We are determined to follow the example set by the Chinese
customs employees and to struggle for justice.

This association wishes to make the following demands :-

1) That the entire body of Chinese employees of the Customs from
the commissioners down to the sailors and porters be
united for the purpose of struggling against the traitors
and national betrayers. They must persist in
pages.zh:
传单译文

上海学生支持海关职员反对伪组织接管海关的宣言。

5月8日，全体中国职员开始了反对伪组织接管海关的光荣而神圣的斗争。本会认为，这场斗争是我们爱国和爱自由的人民对抗占领了我国大片领土、屠杀了大量同胞、并意图奴役整个中华民族的日本帝国主义者的斗争。这场斗争也是我们忠诚勇敢的人民对抗汉奸和卖国贼的斗争。本会特此声明，上海每一位中国公民都有责任与汉奸组成的任何伪组织作斗争。海关的中国职员是上海三百万人民的先锋。这场斗争是这些海关职员响应三百万人民的要求而发起的。我们大、中、小学的成千上万名学生决心不让汉奸和卖国贼在上海活动，也不允许他们通过诡计实现接管海关的目的。我们发誓支持值得我们尊敬的中国海关职员。

关税是我国国民收入的主要来源，而上海海关是中国进出口贸易的关键。因此，上海海关的收入构成了我国国民收入的主要部分。入侵者唆使与伪组织有关的民族败类试图接管海关。如果我们上海市民不保护海关，任由日本入侵者接管，结果将是：(1) 国民政府在财政上遭受损失，导致抵抗力减弱；(2) 日本入侵者将修改关税税则，以破坏中国的进出口贸易；(3) 日本入侵者能够补充其因正在进行的持久战而日益枯竭的军费。本会认为，防止日本入侵者实现其目标是上海每一位中国公民的责任。公告（见中国海关职员发表的宣言）称，他们决心不与任何损害国家和民族利益的伪组织合作，并反对将关税收入存入横滨正金银行，这代表了我们的要求。

今天，5月10日，当我们看到残酷的日本人强行逮捕缉私员杨文龙（Yang Wen Loong，音译）先生时，我们立即知道了日本帝国主义者是多么狡猾和无耻。我们决心效仿中国海关职员的榜样，为正义而斗争。

本会提出以下要求：-

1) 海关全体中国职员，从税务司到水手和搬运工，应团结起来，目的是与汉奸和卖国贼作斗争。他们必须坚持
