TRANSLATION

Important manifesto issued by the Various Circles in
Shanghai to support the arrested Customs Employees

Dear Brethren in Shanghai:

In the eventful month of May, and in the suffocative
city of Shanghai, the Chinese members of the Customs are
beginning to unfurl a "large banner to oppose traitors" and
to light a "torch of non-cooperation." For the sake of
preserving the independence and integrity of the Customs,
they have commenced a struggle against the killers of
mankind and their shameless puppets. This episode has
aroused the sympathy of the whole world. It has also
aroused the antagonistic feelings of the people in this
isolated island against the enemy. On the other hand,
the raising of the banner against traitors and the lighting
of the torch for non-cooperation have served to incite
the brutal enemy to action.

At 11 a.m., May, Mr. Yang Wen Loong, a revenue guard
of the Customs, was kidnapped by persons of a certain
country, while attending to his duty in the Customs shed.
At 11.30 a.m., May 11, Mr. Chang Hung Kwei, an assistant
of the Customs, was also kidnapped in a similar way. These
terroristic acts reveal the brutality and cruelty of people
of that country. In view of these outrages, the people
in Shanghai can no longer live in peace and their lives
are in danger. If no attempt is made to oppose and
struggle against these outrages, the felonious and hellish
hand will reach every one of us who are unwilling to be
slaves.

For the sake of preserving the safety of the people in
Shanghai and protecting the financial bulwark in the form
of the customs, we wish to rally the brethren of Shanghai
in support of the arrested customs employees.

"Protect the integrity of the Customs!

Preserve the confidence of the domestic and foreign
creditors in the Customs! "

译文

上海各界为支持被捕海关职员发表的重要宣言

上海的各位同胞：

在这个多事的五月，在这令人窒息的上海城，海关华员正开始展开“反奸大旗”，点燃“不合作火炬”。为了维护海关的独立与完整，他们已开始同人类杀手及其无耻傀儡进行斗争。这一事件引起了全世界的同情。它也激起了这座孤岛民众对敌人的敌忾之情。另一方面，举起反奸旗帜和点燃不合作火炬也激怒了残暴的敌人采取行动。

5月某日上午11时，海关缉私员杨文龙（Yang Wen Loong，音译）先生在海关棚屋执勤时，被某国人士绑架。5月11日上午11时30分，海关助理张洪贵（Chang Hung Kwei，音译）先生也以类似方式被绑架。这些恐怖行径揭示了该国人的残暴与冷酷。鉴于这些暴行，上海人民已无法安居乐业，生命受到威胁。如果不试图反对并与这些暴行作斗争，那只罪恶且地狱般的手将伸向我们每一个不愿做奴隶的人。

为了保障上海市民的安全，保护作为财政屏障的海关，我们希望号召上海同胞支持被捕的海关职员。

“维护海关完整！

保持国内外债权人对海关的信心！”

Subject Customs employees "talk-kung" strike.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by

As a protest against the assumption of control of the
Customs by the Nanking Reformed Government, some 300 outdoor
staff of the Customs (tidewaiters and revenue guards) declared
a "tai-kung" strike at 6.40 a.m. on May 7, 1938, and were
later joined by some 1,200 indoor staff.

At 10 a.m. the same date, some 500 of the staff held
a meeting in the Dining Hall on the 1st floor of the Customs
Building, The Bund. Mr. L.H. Lawford, Commissioner, and
Mr. Chiu Tsao Chi (裘其), Deputy Commissioner, attended
the meeting and were presented with the following two demands:-

1. That the revenue collected by the Shanghai Customs be
deposited with the Central Bank of China or with the
Hongkong - Shanghai Banking Corporation.

2. That the Custom House continue to fly the National
emblem instead of the five barred flag.

Mr. L.H. Lawford, in reply, stated that he was not in
a position to give an answer to the first demand but assured
the staff that the five barred flag would not be flown over
Custom House for the time being. Mr. Lawford also urged
the staff to resume work forthwith.

Mr. Chiu Tsao Chi, Deputy Commissioner, then took
the chair, and made a speech in which he explained his
attitude stating that he would not compromise in the matter
and would prefer to resign should a satisfactory result not
be arrived at.

After they had spoken, both commissioners retired, while
the staff conducted discussions and decided to organize a

同日早上10时，约500名职员在外滩海关大楼一楼餐厅举行会议。税务司 L.H. Lawford 先生和副税务司裘其（Chiu Tsao Chi）先生出席了会议，并向他们提出了以下两项要求：-

1. 上海海关征收的税款应存入中国银行或汇丰银行。

2. 海关大楼应继续悬挂国徽，而非五色旗。

May 7th, 38.

M.I.C. 460/38.

The Dissension among the Chinese Staff
of the Chinese Maritime Customs.

At 10.15a.m. on 7-5-38 a number of the Chinese
staff about 300 of the Maritime Customs assembled in
the Customs House and tendered either their resignation
or an application for transfer to Chinese controlled
territory.

（印：6 MAY 1938）

It was learnt by the undersigned that owing to
the recent appointment by the Reformed Government of
China (維新政府) of Mr. Lee Kyi Nan (李基南) as Chinese
Supt. of Customs in Shanghai, the Chinese staff have
shown unwillingness to work under the present conditions
and have expressed their dissatisfaction at the
appointment.

A meeting was held at 12noon in the Customs
Building at which Mr. Liang Nyoh Gee (梁若愚), a senior
employee, addressed those present and exhorted them to
continue their work. Until a late hour, however, no
arrangement had been arrived at.

Sen.Det.1/c.

Customs Men
Still Await
Instructions

Chinese Staff Decides
To Carry On Until
Word Received

MEETING HELD
HERE YESTERDAY

Hankow Requested For
Status Definition
Of Workers

Packing every square inch of
pace at the small Customs Club
premises at 10, Lane 479 Bubbling
Well Road yesterday morning, more
than 600 members of the Chinese
Maritime Customs' indoor and out-
door staffs agreed to carry on the
normal routine work of the organ-
ization pending a reply from Han-
kow to their cable.

On Saturday, upon the announce-
ment that the Nanking puppet re-
gime had assumed control of the
Customs, a "go-slow" strike was
declared by Chinese members of the
staff. Subsequently, a cable was sent
to Hankow, requesting that the
Central Government define the
status of the Chinese staff and
give orders as to the line of action
which should be adopted by Chinese
employees in Shanghai.

Officials Preside

Yesterday morning's meeting was
presided over by Deputy Commis-
sioner Chiu Tso-chi and Mr. Ting
Kwei-tang, head of the Chinese
secretariat, both of whom spoke in
the packed clubroom, advising the
continuing of normal routine, pend-
ing a reply to the telegram from
the government, and pointing out
that this attitude would be the
safest and most sensible.

Despite the large body of men
gathered at the meeting, there was
no disorder of any sort—and follow-
ing their decision to hang out the
"business as usual" sign, the em-
ployees dispersed

Saturday Situation

Saturday morning Chinese em-
ployees arriving to work read the
announcement of the "Reformed
Government" spokesmen that the
puppet administration had assumed
control of the Customs. By 9 a.m.
the Chinese outdoor staff declared
a "go-slow" strike by refusing to go
on duty. Gathering in the large
dining room of the Customs House,
the outdoor workers were later
joined by the office staff.

A meeting was called to discuss
the attitude to be adopted and at
10 a.m. Mr. L. H. Lawford, Com-
missioner, and Mr. Chiu Tso-chi,
Deputy Commissioner, joined the
meeting in an effort to urge the
workers to return.

Their efforts were crowned with
the success of logical argument, and
it was decided that a cable seeking
orders direct from the Central
Government should be sent—but
that operations should continue
normally, though "under protest,"
until such orders arrived.

（批：S / 22 9/5）
（批：Liu C.Y.P. 8/9/5）

海关人员
仍在等待
指示

华员决定
在收到消息前
继续工作

昨日在此
举行会议

要求汉口方面
界定员工
身份

昨天上午，超过600名中国海关内勤和外勤员工挤满了位于静安寺路479弄10号狭小的海关俱乐部 premises 的每一寸空间，他们同意在等待汉口方面回复其电报期间，继续维持该机构的日常常规工作。

周六，随着南京傀儡政权宣布接管海关的消息发布，华籍员工宣布实行“怠工”罢工。随后，一份电报发往汉口，请求中央政府界定中国员工的身份，并就上海华籍雇员应采取的行动方针下达指令。

官员主持

昨日上午的会议由副税务司邱作之（Chiu Tso-chi）和华文秘书处处长丁贵堂（Ting Kwei-tang）主持，两人均在拥挤的俱乐部会议室发言，建议在等待政府回电期间继续正常日常工作，并指出这种态度是最安全、最明智的。

尽管参加会议的人数众多，但现场没有任何混乱——在决定挂出“照常营业”的牌子后，员工们便散去了。

周六的情况

周六早晨，前来上班的中国员工 read 到了“维新政府”发言人关于傀儡行政当局已接管海关的公告。到上午9点，中国外勤员工以拒绝上岗的方式宣布实行“怠工”罢工。外勤工人聚集在海关大楼的大餐厅里，随后办公室职员也加入了他们。

随即召开会议讨论应采取的态度，上午10点，税务司 L. H. Lawford 先生和副税务司邱作之先生加入会议，努力敦促工人复工。

他们的努力因合乎逻辑的论证而取得成功，会议决定发送一份直接向中央政府寻求指令的电报——但在收到此类指令之前，行动应“在抗议下”正常继续。

（批：S / 22 9/5）
（批：Liu C.Y.P. 8/9/5）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
（印：SECRET）
S.I. Special Branch Station,
File No. 8218 / 38
Date April 21, 19 38.

Subject Taking over of Chinese Maritime Customs at Shanghai
by the Reformed Government of China.
Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.D.

With reference to the attached cutting from the
"Shanghai Times" dated April 17, 1938, I have to state that
so far no official information has been released by the
Japanese Authorities regarding the taking over by the
Reformed Government of China of the Chinese Maritime Customs
at Shanghai. The local Japanese Authorities, however,
appear to have under consideration the taking over and are
negotiating with the interested parties in the matter.
It is the general belief in Japanese circles that the taking
over of the Chinese Maritime Customs in Shanghai by the
Reformed Government will be realized, when the Japanese
Armies in North and Central China join forces, which is
expected to take place in the region of Tsing-Pu Railway
near Hauchow. The amalgamation of the Reformed Government
of China and the Provisional Government in Peking is expected
to take place at the same time.

Report That
Nanking Will
Take Customs

Tokyo Newspaper Says
Reformed Government
Is About To Act

TARIFF REVISION IS
BEING STUDIED

Revenue In Shanghai Now
Showing Substantial
Increase

TOKYO, April 16.—The
Reformed Government will
soon take over the administra-
tion of the Shanghai Maritime
Customs, the well-informed
“Nichi-Nichi” reported to-day.

The Government, the report add-
ed is already studying the tariff
schedule, in preparation for its re-
vision, “so as to enforce a fair and
impartial tariff.”

Pointing to the increase in re-
venue of the Shanghai Customs, the
journal expressed the opinion that
it would become the main source of
revenue of the new Government.
Shanghai Customs revenue in
March, the paper said, totalled
$7,500,000, which was 30 per cent.
of the total revenue of Chinese
Maritime Customs during that
month.

Compared to the average monthly
revenue of $37,000,000 in the first
half of 1937, the March figure is still
small, but it showed an increase of
$5,000,000 over the amount for
September, 1937, and a $3,000,000
gain over the revenue for January,
1938, the daily stated.—Domei.

Tokyo Conversations

TOKYO, April 16.—Sir Robert L.
Craigie, British Ambassador, and
Mr. Kensuke Horinouchi, Vice-
Minister for Foreign Affairs, this
morning had a 90-minute interview.
The subjects discussed were not
disclosed to the press.—Domei.

报道称
南京将
接管海关

东京报纸称
维新政府
即将行动

正在研究
关税修订

上海税收目前
显示大幅
增长

东京，4月16日电。—据消息灵通的《日日新闻》今日报道，维新政府不久将接管上海海关的行政管理。

报道补充说，政府已经在研究税则表，为修订做准备，“以便实施公平公正的关税”。

该报指出上海海关收入增加，并表示认为这将成为新政府的主要收入来源。该报称，上海海关3月份的收入总计为7,500,000元，占当月中国海关总收入的30%。

与1937年上半年平均每月37,000,000元的收入相比，3月份的数据仍然很小，但该日报指出，这一数字比1937年9月的金额增加了5,000,000元，比1938年1月的收入增加了3,000,000元。—同盟社。

东京会谈

东京，4月16日电。—英国大使罗伯特·克雷吉爵士（Sir Robert L. Craigie）与外务次官堀内谦介（Kensuke Horinouchi）先生今天上午进行了90分钟的会谈。讨论的主题未向媒体披露。—同盟社。

Ten cruisers, including the two fire floats of
the Harbour Fire Brigade, of the Chinese Maritime
Customs were detained by the Japanese Authorities,
when the Chinese troops withdrew from the Shanghai area.
In consequence of the disorganization of the service,
about twenty stokers and crew of the two fire floats
were paid off at the end of February, 1938 without
any trouble.

On March 1, 1938, the Chinese Maritime Customs
Authorities issued a notice to the effect that the
employees attached to the remaining eight customs
preventive cruisers and another two vessels now detained
by the Chinese Authorities at Ningpo, whose services are
less than three years, would be dismissed at the end of
the current month, and paid a retiring gratuity according
to the following scale :-

One year's service.             1 month's pay.
Less than two years.            1½ months' pay.
Less than three years.          2 months' pay.

This decision on the part of the authorities, it is said,
will affect 127 out of the 425 employees whose wages
range from $23 to $85 per month.

On learning of this decision, the employees
affected submitted a petition to the Inspectorate-
General of the Maritime Customs requesting the
cancellation of the decision and submitted that

日期：1938年3月15日。
主题：中国海关 - 解雇海关巡艇上的员工
由督察潘连璧（Pan Lien-pih）撰写，由 **〔此处转录不清〕** 转呈

当中国军队从上海地区撤退时，中国海关的十艘巡艇（包括港务消防队的两艘消防船）被日本当局扣留。由于服务体系的混乱，这两艘消防船的大约二十名司炉和船员在1938年2月底被遣散，过程没有任何麻烦。

1938年3月1日，中国海关当局发布通知，大意是：隶属于剩余八艘海关缉私巡艇以及另外两艘目前被中国当局扣留在宁波的船只、服务年限不足三年的员工，将在本月底被解雇，并按以下标准支付退休金：

服务一年。             1个月薪水。
不足两年。            1个半月薪水。
不足三年。          2个月薪水。

据说，当局的这一决定将影响425名员工中的127人，他们的月薪在23元至85元之间。

Subject ......... Chinese Maritime Customs - Sailors discharged.

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken ......... Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Owing to the detention by the Japanese military
of a number of preventive cruisers, the authorities of the
Chinese Maritime Customs discharged on March 1 approximately
twenty sailors. They were paid retiring gratuities
according to the following scale :-

Half month's wages for those who had worked for the
Customs for one year.

One month's wages for those who had worked for two
years.

One and a half months' wages for those who had
worked for three years.

Two months' wages for those who had worked for
over three years.

About twenty sailors held a meeting at 10 a.m.
March 2 in the Customs Employees' Club, Lane 97, 62
Myburgh Road, when the possible discharge of sailors with
less than three years' service was discussed.

There are about 500 sailors in the employ of the
Chinese Maritime Customs.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH - 4 MAR 1938）

由于多艘缉私巡艇被日军扣留，中国海关当局于3月1日解雇了大约二十名水手。他们按以下标准领取了退休金：

在海关工作一年者，发给半个月工资。

工作两年者，发给一个月工资。

工作三年者，发给一个半月工资。

工作三年以上者，发给两个月工资。

大约二十名水手于3月2日上午10点在迈尔西爱路62号97弄的海关员工俱乐部举行会议，讨论了服务年限不足三年的水手可能被解雇的问题。

中国海关雇佣的水手约有500人。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Special Branch - S.B. Station,
REPORT
Date December 24, 1937.

Subject Extract from 'The China Press' of December 23, 1937.

Made by D. S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. S.

With reference to the attached extract from 'The
China Press' dated December 23, 1937, I have to state
that the contents of this article are absolutely incorrect
and misleading and that the story is entirely the figment
of imagination of the newspaper reporter concerned.
Mr. Hiramoto, Chief Tidesurveyer of the Chinese
Maritime Customs, informed the reporter in an interview
that lasted no longer than two minutes, that Japanese
Customs officers were carrying out their duties on all
wharves north of the Creek, and although no arrangements
had been made for foreign officers to carry out the same
duties in the same area, the possibility did exist that
efforts would later be made for these foreign officers
to resume their tasks, but nothing of any definite nature
was mentioned.

Da. Pitts.
CP
D. S.
S.C. (Special Branch).

（左侧批注：DBR 24/12）
（底部批注：File DBR 2072）
（印：24 DEC 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

THE CHINESE CUSTOMS

The local Customs authorities have
transferred 60 of the 100 inspectors to the interior.
160 of the 330 officers of the Customs Police attached
to the Godown Control Office have been paid off. The
Customs Superintendent's Office at No.1333 Jinza Road has
been closed.
